topics: heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties

Situated on the south side of Rosemary Lane southeast of Eglinton Avenue West and Bathurst Street in Forest Hill, the property at 14 Rosemary Lane contains a two-and-a-half-storey, Tudor Revival house built in 1935. City Council is asked to approve the listing.

title: Toronto Local Appeal Body - Chair's 2021 Annual Report
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: This is an information item: the Director of Court Services transmits the Toronto Local Appeal Body Chair's 2021 Annual Report. The TLAB, created May 3, 2017, is the independent quasi-judicial tribunal that hears appeals of Committee of Adjustment decisions on minor variances and consents under the Planning Act. Council is asked to receive the report and the chair's annual report for information; no decision is attached.

title: Update: Building Code Changes to Permit Partial Occupancy of Super Tall Buildings During Construction
topics: building codes;
brief: Toronto Building staff report back on provincial Building Code changes that would allow partial occupancy of super tall buildings still under construction, following the province's April 2022 consultation. Staff recommend Council ask the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing to amend Building Code Article 1.3.3.7 before November 1, 2022 to address municipal risk and monitoring concerns with the draft article.

title: Ready, Set, Midtown: Zoning Review - City Initiated Zoning By-law Amendments for Neighbourhoods Designated Lands within the Avenue Midtown Transit Station Area - Final Report
topics: neighbourhoods, zoning bylaws; cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: As part of 'Ready, Set, Midtown,' the Chief Planner recommends city-initiated zoning by-law amendments to put the Avenue Midtown Transit Station Area policies of the Yonge-Eglinton Secondary Plan (OPA 405) into zoning permissions. The Midtown Zoning Review is one of three initiatives implementing OPA 405, alongside the infrastructure strategy and the parks and public realm strategy. Council is asked to amend By-law 569-2013 and former By-law 438-86 for the affected areas.

title: Christie's Planning Study - City-initiated Secondary Plan and Zoning By-law - Technical Amendments
brief: The Chief Planner recommends technical amendments to the Christie's area Secondary Plan (OPA 506) and area-specific zoning by-law, adopted by Council in May 2021. The bills were held back while the Section 37 agreement was finalized, and revisions became necessary as the applicant prepared detailed Site Plan Control drawings. The report also asks Council to allow tiebacks and to accept on-site parkland. Council is asked to adopt the revised zoning by-law and secondary plan amendments.

title: Prioritizing Affordable Housing in the Development Application Review Process
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher recommends Council ask the Chief Planner, in consultation with the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat, to report to the Planning and Housing Committee in the first quarter of 2023 on how the development application review process could be enhanced to prioritize affordable housing. The request follows a 2019 City-commissioned housing market analysis warning that without government action, low- and moderate-income households will face a grim housing situation. Council is asked to approve the report-back.

title: Employee Talent, Retention and Attraction - City Planning
topics: equity, planning; employment equity; fair wage; pay equity
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Planner reports to the Planning and Housing Committee on strategies to retain and attract City Planning staff, in response to a Council request, prepared in consultation with People and Equity. title: Advancing Affordable and Supportive Housing Projects, Programs and Initiatives
brief: The Housing Secretariat asks Council to approve a package of actions in the coming months to advance affordable and supportive housing under the HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan, including lease and sub-lease authorities for modular supportive housing projects. The source document's recommendations are cut off partway through the first item, so this brief reflects only what the available text establishes. Council is asked to authorize the listed actions.

title: Local Priority Rules for Rent-Geared-to-Income Housing and Centralizing Access for Affordable Rental Housing
topics: affordable housing, rental housing; affordable homes; housing projects, rental properties; rental units

The move responds to the HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan and its Housing Charter, which commit the City to a human-rights-based approach to housing. Council is also asked to set local priority rules for rent-geared-to-income housing.

title: Renoviction Policy - Creating a Framework to Protect Affordable and Mid-range Rental Homes and Deter Renovictions
topics: affordable housing, rental housing; affordable homes; housing projects, rental properties; rental units

The policy responds to the HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan and the City's Housing Charter, which commit the City to preventing eviction-driven homelessness and protecting renters. Council is also asked to direct the Executive Director to report back on by-law development.

These delineations set density targets and planning rules around transit stations. Council is asked to adopt all four amendments.

Council is asked to adopt OPA 591.

brief: Council policy currently bars many forms of communication, including electronic newsletters, between August 1 and election day, and it applies to all councillors whether or not they are running again. Councillor Filion argues this blocks needed outreach, citing refugee housing at 3 Park Home Avenue opening September 1. The motion asks Council to let members who are not seeking re-election, confirmed at the close of nominations, resume publishing to constituents.

brief: Since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, Parks, Forestry and Recreation has provided community centre and park space to Toronto Public Health and health partners for testing and immunization clinics, and to community groups for food security initiatives, with fees waived under the emergency order. This motion asks Council to delegate authority to the General Manager to keep waiving fees for existing permits for these uses. Organizations would still cover extra costs such as staff overtime.

brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends Council direct the General Manager of Transportation Services, in consultation with the Toronto Police Service, to report back in the first quarter of 2023 on impaired driving in Toronto, including traffic collision statistics. Impaired driving is one of Canada's leading causes of vehicle collisions; Mothers Against Drunk Driving estimates 1,250 to 1,500 Canadians are killed in impairment-related crashes each year and 63,000 injured, and survey data showed a 30 percent rise in self-reported drunk driving in 2021. The source document is cut off after the first recommendation.

brief: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson, recommends Council authorize the General Manager of Fleet Services to donate up to two end-of-life Ford Escape vehicles, otherwise destined for auction, to the Ukrainian government at no cost for humanitarian purposes. This adds to two end-of-life Chevrolet Tahoe emergency response vehicles with lights, sirens and first-aid supplies already committed by Toronto Paramedic Services. The Atlantic Ukrainian Association, at the request of Ukraine's Embassy in Canada, will handle shipping the vehicles to Ukraine for emergency response.

The pandemic and rising living costs have increased demand for charity services in mental health, food and hygiene security, while the charities themselves face rising rents: industrial lease rates rose 18.4 percent and commercial-retail rates 38.3 percent from the third quarter of 2020 to the third quarter of 2021. The source document is cut off after the first recommendation.

brief: Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Mayor John Tory, recommends Council authorize the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to contribute and transfer up to $200,000 in 2022 toward Toronto's sponsorship of the 2022 Toronto Global Forum. Organized by the International Economic Forum of the Americas and held in Toronto annually since 2007, the forum draws heads of state, central bank governors, ministers and global economic decision-makers; the City has sponsored it since 2008. The forum brings about $2.2 million in direct spending to Toronto's economy. The source document is cut off after the first recommendation.

Toronto hosts one of the largest Somali communities outside Africa, whose members have contributed to the city's civic, cultural, economic and political life, yet face systemic barriers from anti-Black racism and Islamophobia. The centre would serve programming needs across ages and act as a hub to preserve and celebrate Somali culture. The source document is cut off after the first recommendation.

The Economic Development and Culture Division, Corporate Real Estate Management's St. Lawrence Market and Market CityTO submitted the successful bid; the main organizer is the U.S. not-for-profit Project for Public Spaces. The conference brings together leading public market operators, developers and thought leaders, with the last edition drawing representatives from 113 international cities and 36 countries. brief: This motion asks Council to direct $4,000,000 in Section 37 funds, subject to receipt from the property named in the confidential attachment, to the Toronto Business Development Centre. The money would go toward purchasing, building or improving a property as a skills training hub in Scarborough Southwest serving Scarborough residents and supporting post-COVID recovery. The Centre would prioritize employment and skills programming.

title: Protecting and Promoting biodiversity on Toronto Island - by Councillor Joe Mihevc, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: natural features, parks and open space areas, vegetation; flora; plant life, green spaces; open spaces, landforms
brief: Toronto Island draws about 1.5 million visitors a year, but only 12 percent remains in a natural state, and that area is a biodiversity hotspot on the north shore of Lake Ontario, home to species at risk such as piping plovers and sand dune plant communities found nowhere else on the western shore. This motion asks Council to direct the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation, with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority and stakeholders, to maximize biodiversity protection on the Island.

brief: On July 19, 2022 the Toronto Star reported that Premier Doug Ford would legislate a "strong mayor" system for Toronto, giving the mayor final say on the budget and other matters. This motion argues that would erode local democracy by stifling advocacy on issues affecting Torontonians. It asks Council to request the Province not to implement a strong mayor system with a budget veto or other added mayoral powers.

title: Request for a Vulnerable Road User Safety Review of the Easterly Intersection of Thorncliffe Park Drive and Overlea Boulevard
topics: pedestrians; pedestrianization
brief: This item asks North York Community Council to order an urgent vulnerable road user safety review at the westerly intersection of Thorncliffe Park Drive and Overlea Boulevard. Councillor Jaye Robinson cites the June 16 incident in which an 11-year-old boy sustained life-threatening injuries after being struck by a vehicle at that intersection, in a dense neighbourhood with four local schools and many young families. Council is asked to direct Transportation Services to carry out the review with a focus on increasing pedestrian crossing safety.

Councillor Jaye Robinson launched the plan in 2019 to tackle vehicle speeds, compliance, and traffic infiltration in Leaside, but phase-one consultation was delayed when staff were redeployed for the pandemic response. Council is asked to direct the report.

brief: The Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer Advisory Committee asks City Council to direct the General Manager of Seniors Services and Long-Term Care to address reported homophobia and neglect affecting 2SLGBTQI+ seniors in one of the City's ten long-term care homes, where conditions are harming residents' daily lives. The committee also notes the “Diversity our Strength” 2SLGBTQI+ training tool kit is not being used in the City's long-term care homes. title: Feasibility of Establishing a City of Toronto Unit Responsible for 2SLGBTQ+ Issues
body: Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer Advisory Committee
brief: The Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer Advisory Committee asks City Council to investigate the feasibility of a dedicated City unit for 2SLGBTQ+ issues. Many equity-deserving groups in the City's Equity Lens Toolkit have a dedicated unit or office — the Indigenous Affairs Office, the Gender Equity Unit, the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Unit — but 2SLGBTQ+ communities appear to lack one, and dedicated staff support is needed to follow through on committee recommendations. The committee recommends Council ask the City Manager to investigate the feasibility of a dedicated City of Toronto unit.

title: Construction Staging Area - 838-880 Dupont Street and 1080 Shaw Street
topics: construction; building

The request covers closing the north sidewalk on Dupont Street between Shaw Street and a point 144 metres west, from May 12, 2022 to May 31, 2025. Because the TTC operates transit service on Dupont Street, City Council approval is required. Council is asked to approve the staging area.

title: 545 Lake Shore Boulevard West Zoning Amendment - Final Report
topics: rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment for 545 Lake Shore Boulevard West to permit a mixed-use development with residential, office, and retail uses. The designated heritage Crosse and Blackwell building on the north portion of the site would be conserved and re-used for office purposes, with residential and retail uses in new 13- and 21-storey buildings on the south portion. Council is asked to amend the Zoning By-law.

title: 181 Sterling Road (Block 4B of 158 Sterling Road) - Zoning By-law Amendment Application (Removal of the Holding Symbol "h") - Final Report
topics: mixed use areas, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend Zoning By-law 943-2015 (OMB) to remove the holding symbol from a portion of the lands at 181 Sterling Road (Block 4B of 158 Sterling Road). Removing the “h” would permit a 16-storey mixed-use building with non-residential uses on the first and second floors, as the conditions for lifting the hold have been met. Council is asked to approve the amendment.

title: 1488 Queen Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment for 1488 Queen Street West to permit a six-storey (25 metres including mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building with 29 residential units and commercial uses at grade. The proposal is consistent with the Provincial Policy Statement (2020) and the Growth Plan. Council is asked to amend Zoning By-law 569-2013.

title: 5, 7, 9, 11, 15 and 19 Cosburn Avenue and 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 30, 32, 34, 36, 38 and 40 Gowan Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Request for Direction Report

Council is asked to authorize the opposition.

title: 137-149 Church Street - Zoning Amendment Application - Request for Direction Report
topics: planning, zoning;
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and appropriate staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in support of the revised zoning by-law amendment application for 137-149 Church Street. Submitted June 2018 and revised to include 137 Church Street, the proposal is now a 54-storey mixed-use development with ground-floor commercial uses, 469 dwelling units, and 31,688 square metres of gross floor area. Council is asked to authorize the settlement support.

title: 102 Berkeley Street - Zoning Amendment Application - Request for Direction Report
topics: zoning bylaws, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and appropriate staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the zoning by-law amendment appeal for 102 Berkeley Street. Submitted October 2021, the application proposed a 20-storey mixed-use building with 357 square metres of ground-floor retail and 181 dwelling units above; the applicant appealed in January 2022 citing Council's failure to decide within the 90-day Planning Act timeframe. Council is asked to authorize the opposition.

title: Temporary Street Parking Relocation on Parliament Street from Carlton Street to South of Winchester Street for Cabbagetown Naturescape, a Ten-Week Summer Festival to Promote Economic Recovery from COVID-19
topics: parking;
brief: Staff ask City Council to support the Cabbagetown Naturescape, a ten-week outdoor public realm festival on Parliament Street from Carlton Street to south of Winchester Street, meant to promote economic recovery from COVID-19. The street would be animated with natural features — logs, stones, tree canopy, and other plantings — to create a safe, natural, comfortable public space. Council is asked to rescind the existing parking machine regulation ($3.00 per hour, maximum three hours, 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. Monday to Saturday and 1 p.m. to 9 p.m. Sunday) on the east side of Parliament Street to allow the festival.

title: Inclusion on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register - Dundas-Carlaw Properties
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend City Council include nine properties with cultural heritage value on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register, in line with the March 14, 2022 listing statements. The recommendation responds to Toronto and East York Community Council's October 2021 request for an update on heritage reports for historic industrial buildings in the Carlaw-Dundas Study Area. The community council is asked to endorse the recommendation to Council.

brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment for 406 and 410 Keele Street to permit a 5-storey residential building with 65 dwelling units and 32 vehicle parking spaces in one level of underground parking. The application is consistent with the Provincial Policy Statement (2020) and the Growth Plan. Council is asked to amend Zoning By-law 438-86 for the lands.

Council makes the final appointments. No final appointment is made at this step.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Clerk asks the Striking Committee to consider members' preferences and recommend to City Council the appointment of two Council Members to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors, for a term starting at the 2022 annual meeting. Council makes the final appointments. No final appointment is made at this step.

title: Final Report - 113 to 141 Montezuma Trail - Zoning By-Law Amendment Application
topics: planning, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve zoning amendments for 113 to 141 Montezuma Trail to permit 81 residential dwelling units and 296 square metres of commercial uses. A previous application to rezone the lands was approved by Council in 2019. Council is asked to amend City Zoning By-law 569-2013 and Agincourt North Scarborough Zoning By-law 12797.

title: Final Report - 3459 to 3471 Sheppard Avenue East  - Zoning Amendment Application
topics: planning, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment for 3459-3471 Sheppard Avenue East to permit a 12-storey (38.6-metre) mixed-use development, demolishing the existing commercial plaza. The mid-rise building would contain 205 residential units and 17,819 square metres of gross floor area, at 4.83 times the area of the lot. Council is asked to amend Zoning By-law 569-2013.

title: Final Report - 2567 Eglinton Avenue East - Zoning By-law Amendment Application
topics: planning, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment for 2567 Eglinton Avenue East to permit an 11-storey mixed-use building with 8,856 square metres of gross floor area and 118 dwelling units. The ground floor would have 432 square metres of retail and commercial space, at a floor space index of about 3.25. Council is asked to amend Zoning By-law 569-2013.

title: U-turn prohibition McNicoll Avenue immediately west of Kennedy Road
topics: turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: Councillor Nick Mantas asks Scarborough Community Council to prohibit westbound U-turns at all times on McNicoll Avenue between a point about 200 metres west of Kennedy Road and a point 120 metres further west, near 1881-1883 McNicoll Avenue, responding to numerous community concerns. Because the TTC operates transit service on McNicoll Avenue, City Council approval is required. The community council is asked to endorse the recommendation to Council.

title: Tilley Drive Traffic Concerns
topics: traffic, transportation; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to address traffic concerns on Tilley Drive, responding to Scarborough Community Council's request to investigate speed and volume measures in conjunction with the Port Union Road Improvements Project (SC27.10). Staff recommend prohibiting eastbound and westbound through traffic movements at all times at the intersection of Port Union Road and Tilley Drive and the private driveway. Council is asked to approve the prohibition.

title: Pay-and-Display Parking - Kingston Road
topics: metered parking spaces, transportation; metered street parking; parking stalls, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services and the Toronto Parking Authority ask City Council to authorize new pay-and-display on-street parking locations on Kingston Road in Ward 20. TPA worked with Transportation Services to identify spaces that will support the local community and area businesses by encouraging turnover in the on-street parking supply. Because the TTC operates transit service on Kingston Road, City Council approval is required. Council is asked to authorize the parking regulation amendments in Attachments 1 and 2.

title: Final Report - 250 Danforth Road - Zoning Amendment and Subdivision Applications
topics: planning, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the zoning amendment and subdivision applications for 250 Danforth Road — a 10-storey (220-unit) mixed-use building fronting Danforth Road, 70 stacked townhouse units, and 21 regular townhouse units, with Dairy Drive and Bamblett Drive extended by a proposed 16.5-metre public street. The proposal is consistent with the Provincial Policy Statement (2020) and the Growth Plan. Council is asked to amend Zoning By-law 569-2013.

title: Metrolinx Scarborough Subway Extension - Scarborough Centre GO Bus Relocation
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, subway stations, transportation; transportation services, ttc
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to approve temporarily relocating six GO Transit bus bays to the east side of Borough Drive between Progress Avenue and Triton Road. Metrolinx GO buses and intercity buses currently operate from the TTC Scarborough Centre Station at 290 Borough Drive, but must move in fall 2022 because the TTC needs the terminal space to run additional service for the Scarborough Subway Extension. Because the TTC operates transit service on Borough Drive, City Council approval is required. Council is asked to approve the temporary relocation.
address: 290 Borough Toronto Ontario; Toronto Ontario McCowan Bushby

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2537, 280 Manse Road, Manse Developments Inc.
topics: assumption of services;
brief: This is a procedural item: staff ask City Council to authorize the City to assume the municipal road and services installed under the subdivision agreement between Manse Developments Inc. and the City for registered Plan of Subdivision 66M-2537 at 280 Manse Road. Council is asked to approve the assumption.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Scarborough Community Preservation Panel
topics: appointments, heritage preservation, planning; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: This is a procedural item: Scarborough Community Council considers the appointment of public members to the Scarborough Community Preservation Panel. The report deals with personal matters about identifiable individuals being considered for appointment. The community council is asked to approve the appointments.

title: Woodside Square Planning Review - Proposals Report
topics: planning, proposals; bids; request for proposal; rfp
brief: This is an information item: City Planning staff provide a status update on the Woodside Square Planning Review and present policy directions for a future Site and Area Specific Policy for the site, for upcoming public consultation. The review responds to current policy direction for 1571 Sandhurst Circle (Woodside Square Mall), designated a Special Policy Area. The community council is asked to direct the Chief Planner to use the draft policy directions in the April 4, 2022 report.

title: City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendments to Implement Scarborough Subway Extension - Final Report
topics: subway routes, transportation, zoning; transportation services
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve City-initiated zoning by-law amendments to facilitate delivery of the Scarborough Subway Extension. The amendments would provide relief from certain zoning provisions related to transportation uses for lands Metrolinx will acquire for project elements such as stations and support structures. Council is asked to amend City Zoning By-law 569-2013 and the former Scarborough Employment Districts Zoning By-law 24982.

brief: This is a procedural item: the City Council meeting opens with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: Open Door Affordable Rental Housing Support for 28 New Affordable Rental Homes at 90 and 100 Simcoe Street, 130 Pearl Street, and 203, 207 and 211 Adelaide Street West
topics: affordable housing, rental housing; affordable homes; housing projects, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Open Door Affordable Rental Housing Program incentives for 28 new affordable rental homes in the redevelopment of 90 and 100 Simcoe Street, 130 Pearl Street, and 203, 207, and 211 Adelaide Street West (“100 Simcoe Street”). The affordable homes would be part of a larger mixed-use development with an additional 498 purpose-built rental units. The Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat recommends Council authorize the 28 units for waivers of planning application, building permit, parkland dedication, and development charge fees. Council is asked to approve the incentives.

title: Delivering Affordable Rental Housing at 1113-1117 Dundas Street West
topics: development, housing; developing land; development (land); land development, homes; residences
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize transferring $459,745, inclusive of HST and disbursements, from the Section 37 Reserve Fund to the Capital Revolving Reserve Fund for Affordable Housing to deliver affordable rental housing at 1113-1117 Dundas Street West. The transfer advances the HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan's actions across the housing continuum. Council is asked to approve the transfer.

title: Dundas-Sherbourne Neighbourhood Revitalization - Update
topics: affordable housing, community & life (sc), health (sc), housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: This is an information item: the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat updates the Planning and Housing Committee on the Dundas-Sherbourne neighbourhood revitalization. Given persistent, systemic housing, health, social, economic, and safety challenges for residents of 251 Sherbourne Street (the Dan Harrison Community Complex) and the wider community, Council directed the City, Toronto Community Housing, and CreateTO in March 2021 (PH21.2) to report back. The committee is asked to direct further work on the revitalization.

title: Amendment to the Effective Date of Mandatory Pre-Application Consultation By-law 46-2022
topics: land, municipal codes, official plan amendments; property
brief: The Chief Planner asks City Council to amend the effective date of Section 3 of By-law 46-2022, which established mandatory pre-application consultation as a prerequisite for a complete development application in Toronto. Council adopted the Official Plan amendment and Municipal Code amendment on February 3, 2022; with no appeals during the appeal period, the Official Plan amendment came into full force on March 8, 2022. Council is asked to approve the date change.

title: Modular Housing Initiative: Phase Two - 175 Cummer Avenue - City Initiated Rezoning - Final Report
topics: housing, rezoning; homes; residences, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a City-initiated zoning by-law amendment for 175 Cummer Avenue to permit a low-rise residential apartment under the Modular Housing Initiative Phase Two. Council directed the municipal rezoning on March 9, 2022, after previously asking the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing for a Minister's Zoning Order. Council is asked to amend City Zoning By-law 569-2013.

title: Our Plan Toronto: Keele-St. Clair Local Area Study - Final Recommendation Report
topics: land use, official plan amendments;
brief: Staff recommend City Council create a new Secondary Plan for the Keele-St. Clair area following the Keele-St. Clair Local Area Study under the Our Plan Toronto review. The report recommends amending the Official Plan's Chapter 6 (Secondary Plans), Chapter 7 (Site and Area Specific Policies), Map 2 (Urban Structure), Map 17 (Land Use), Map 35 (Secondary Plan Key), and Schedule 2 (planned but unbuilt roads). Council is asked to amend the Official Plan as in Attachment 1 and authorize the City Solicitor.

title: 50 Merton Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, property (sc);
brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the property at 50 Merton Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The Girl Guides of Canada Headquarters there was the organization's first permanent, purpose-built national headquarters since its founding in Canada in 1910 — a three-storey Post-War Modern complex completed in 1962 to the design of Carmen Corneil and extended in 1970-72 by Elin and Carmen Corneil. The Planning and Housing Committee is asked to endorse the recommendation to Council.

title: 1702 Queen Street East - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, property (sc);
brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the property at 1702 Queen Street East under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. On the northwest corner of Queen Street East and Kingston Road in the Woodbine Beach precinct, the property contains the Imperial Bank of Canada Building — a two-storey bank building on a raised basement with a one-storey wing, built in 1911-12 to the designs of Toronto architects Sharp & Brown. The Planning and Housing Committee is asked to endorse the recommendation to Council.

title: 221 Sterling Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation;
brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the property at 221 Sterling Road (including active entrances at 225 and 227 Sterling Road) under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property comprises a complex of adjoining one- and two-storey brick structures built incrementally around 1914-1918 and 1924-1939. Council is asked to state its intention to designate.

title: 2600-2700 Steeles Avenue West, City of Vaughan - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Request for Direction Report
topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: This is an information item: staff respond to development applications filed in the City of Vaughan for 2600-2700 Steeles Avenue West, which were circulated to the City of Toronto under the Planning Act given the site's proximity to the municipal border. The report sets out City Planning staff's comments and recommendations on further action. The Chief Planner recommends Council forward the report to Vaughan's Development Planning Department and take a position if Vaughan approves the applications. Council is asked to approve the direction.

title: City of Toronto Review of Bill 109: More Homes for Everyone Act, 2022
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Planner updates the Planning and Housing Committee on the City's review of Bill 109, the More Homes for Everyone Act, 2022. After the Province published the Housing Affordability Task Force report on February 8, 2022 with 55 recommendations, the Province introduced Bill 109 on March 30, 2022 with changes to the Planning Act and the City of Toronto Act. The committee is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Request to Explore the PARTNA Program and Alternative Affordable Housing Options
topics: affordable housing, land use, racial discrimination, zoning; affordable homes; housing projects, anti-racism; racism
brief: The Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee asks City Council to direct the Chief Planner and the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat to work with the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration to explore the PARTNA program and alternative affordable housing options. The advisory committee considered item CR6.2 at its April 1, 2022 meeting. Council is asked to approve the direction.

title: Technical Amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013
topics: legislation, municipal officials, zoning bylaws; acts, city officials, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Chief Planner asks City Council to enact technical amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013 — correcting typographical errors, adding, removing, or replacing words, revising regulations to clarify or correct interpretations and permissions, and adjusting zoning and overlay map boundaries. Technical changes are also proposed to By-laws 941-2021 and 366-2020, which amended the main by-law, to correct errors. Council is asked to enact the amendments and authorize the City Solicitor to make stylistic changes.

title: 4155 Yonge Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Direction

brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and appropriate staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in support of a settlement for the Official Plan and zoning by-law amendment appeal for 4155 Yonge Street. Submitted October 2017, the application proposed a 14-storey residential building with 64 units, 82 underground parking spaces, and 49 bicycle spaces, at 10,312.5 square metres of gross floor area. Council is asked to authorize the settlement support.

title: 500 Duplex Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Direction
topics: planning approvals; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and appropriate staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the zoning by-law amendment appeal for 500 Duplex Avenue. Submitted July 2021, the application proposed two infill residential rental buildings — 11 storeys (37.4 metres) and 15 storeys (48.4 metres), each with a 5-metre mechanical penthouse — adding 45,416 square metres of residential floor area beside the existing 34-storey rental apartment building, which would remain. Council is asked to authorize the opposition.

title: 6150 to 6160 Yonge Street, 9 to 11 Pleasant Avenue and 18 Goulding Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Final Report
topics: planning approvals; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning by-law amendments for 6150 to 6160 Yonge Street, 9 to 11 Pleasant Avenue, and 18 Goulding Avenue, to permit a thirteen-storey residential building with ground-floor retail. The building would have 577 residential units and 299 vehicle parking spaces including 57 visitor spaces, with 44,829 square metres of gross floor area at a floor space index of 5.83. Council is asked to amend the Official Plan and zoning by-laws.

title: 105 Sheppard Avenue East, 24 and 26 Leona Drive - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: official plan amendments, redevelopment, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning by-law amendments for 105 Sheppard Avenue East and 24 and 26 Leona Drive, to permit an 8-storey (28.5-metre) mixed-use building with 58 residential units above ground-floor retail, at 4,550 square metres of gross floor area and a floor space index of 3.12. The 48 parking spaces would sit in a two-level underground garage. Council is asked to amend the Official Plan and zoning by-law.

title: 196 Valley Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Final Report
topics: planning approvals; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment for 196 Valley Road to permit six townhouse units fronting Bayview Avenue. The units form one block, three storeys and 11 metres high, with vehicle access via a 6.0-metre north-south private driveway from Valley Road and 12 parking spaces at the rear. Council is asked to amend former North York Zoning By-law 7625 and City Zoning By-law 569-2013.

brief: Staff recommend City Council approve zoning amendments for 1629 Sheppard Avenue West to permit seven 3-storey (13-metre) residential units in three sets of semi-detached houses and one detached house fronting Sheppard Avenue West. brief: This is a procedural item: North York Community Council considers appointments of public members to the North York Community Preservation Panel. title: 1377 Sheppard Avenue West - Plan of Subdivision Application - Final Report

brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Planner advises City Council, under delegated approval authority (By-law 229-2000), of the intent to approve the draft plan of subdivision for 1377 Sheppard Avenue West. No Council decision is required.

brief: CentreCourt Development asks City Council to approve a construction staging area for its 14-storey mixed-use development at 1100 Sheppard Avenue West. Because the TTC operates transit service on Kodiak Crescent, City Council approval is required. Council is asked to approve the staging area.

title: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 Oakburn Crescent - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Direction

brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and appropriate staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the Official Plan and zoning by-law amendment appeal for 2 to 12 Oakburn Crescent. Council is asked to authorize the opposition.

title: 48, 50, 56, 58 and 60 Avondale Avenue, 17 and 19 Bales Avenue and 25, 35, 37, 39, 41, 43, 45, 51, 53 and 55 Glendora Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Direction
topics: planning approvals; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and appropriate staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the Official Plan, zoning by-law, and rental housing demolition appeals for 48-60 Avondale Avenue, 17-19 Bales Avenue, and 25-55 Glendora Avenue. Submitted August 2021, the application proposed demolishing 16 detached dwellings for three tall residential buildings of 40, 37, and 26 storeys (124.25, 113.90, and 80.85 metres) with 1,046 residential units. Council is asked to authorize the opposition.

title: 3621 Dufferin Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Final Report
topics: planning approvals; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the zoning by-law amendment and draft plan of subdivision applications for 3621 Dufferin Street — a 10-storey (40-metre, with a 13-metre tall marquee feature) mixed-use development with 153 residential units, retail, office, and self-storage uses, and 334 vehicle and 161 bicycle parking spaces in a three-level underground garage. Council is asked to amend City Zoning By-law 569-2013 and authorize the subdivision.

title: 5800 Yonge Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Request for Direction
topics: official plan amendments, redevelopment, rezoning, subdivision (land), zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization, subdivision of land
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor asks City Council for direction on the Official Plan amendment, zoning by-law amendment, and draft plan of subdivision applications for 5800 Yonge Street. Submitted January 31, 2020, the applications propose 34- and 37-storey residential towers on individual base buildings, plus 37- and 44-storey residential towers linked by a 2- and 4-storey base building with residential, retail, and office uses. Council is asked to adopt the confidential recommendations.

title: Creating New Affordable Housing with Supports for Indigenous Men at 218 Carlton Street - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: First Nations, affordable housing, social housing; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, affordable homes; housing projects, community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units
brief: Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to create new affordable housing with supports for Indigenous men at 218 Carlton Street. In July 2019 (TE7.15) Council authorized a Section 37 agreement with MOD Developments securing the transfer of the 218 Carlton Street property to the City at no cost for affordable housing. Council is asked to authorize the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat to provide $550,000, inclusive of HST and disbursements, from the Capital Revolving Reserve Fund for Affordable Housing (XR1058).

title: Technical Amendment to By-law 569-2013 Regarding 2740 Lawrence Avenue East - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, asks City Council to enact a technical amendment to Zoning By-law 569-2013 for 2740 Lawrence Avenue East. In July 2021 Council approved rezoning the former David and Mary Thomson Collegiate Institute lands for a new residential subdivision with 35 detached dwellings. Council is asked to enact the zoning amendment in Attachment 1 to the motion and to determine that the revisions are minor and technical.

title: Authorization to extend the InTO the Ravines partnership with Park People - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: ravines; ravine protection areas
brief: Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to extend the InTO the Ravines partnership with Park People. In January 2020 Council directed the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to develop the InTO Ravines program with the national registered charity Park People, and it launched that fall to connect residents with ravine nature. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager to extend the program to December 31, 2022.

title: Getting Etobicoke Transit Back on Track - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday, asks City Council to get Etobicoke transit back on track. Between 2016 and 2021, Etobicoke-Lakeshore's population grew 9.8 percent — the second-largest growth rate in Toronto — and managing that growth needs significant transit investment; Humber Bay Shores shows what happens when rapid growth outruns transit. Council is asked to request the Executive Director of Transit Expansion and the Chief Planner, with the TTC, to report to the Executive Committee on transit priorities for the area.

title: Enjoying a Drink Outdoors: Providing Safe, Responsible and Equitable Options for All - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: equity, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, employment equity; fair wage; pay equity
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, asks City Council to approve a pilot project allowing the consumption of alcoholic beverages of up to 15 percent alcohol by volume in City parks and beaches that have bathrooms. Over the pandemic, Torontonians embraced outdoor socializing, and Council loosened patio restrictions through the CaféTO program, now in its third year; the motion seeks safe, responsible, and equitable options for drinking outdoors beyond backyards and balconies. Council is asked to approve the pilot.

title: Cancellation of Security Guards at 6 City Parks - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: parks, security guards; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to defer spending on security guards at six City parks until Council is fully briefed. The City has issued a request for proposals for contracted security to watch its parks, with guards reporting any illegal tent or structure immediately. Council is asked to direct that the spending be deferred until Council has been fully briefed on a variety of options, including spending on connecting people with spaces where they can stay instead of living outdoors.

title: 1792 Danforth Avenue - Café TO Temporary Outdoor Patio Deck - Technical Amendment to Municipal Code Chapter 742 - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: municipal codes, restaurants; cafeterias; dining; eating places; food premises
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, asks City Council to make a technical amendment to Municipal Code Chapter 742 for the restaurant at 1792 Danforth Avenue. CaféTO and outdoor dining have been a lifeline for local restaurants during the pandemic, and the establishment is applying for a sidewalk café permit to formalize its long-existing deck patio. Council is asked to request the Executive Director of Municipal Licensing and Standards to act on a sidewalk café application for the address under Chapter 742.

title: More than Window Shopping: Exploring Opportunities to Support Small Businesses Facing Vandalized Windows - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Paula Fletcher
topics: business improvement areas, vandalism; bia; business improvement associations
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Paula Fletcher, asks City Council to explore ways to support small businesses facing vandalized windows. East End Business Improvement Areas have seen more incidents of vandalism and damage to storefront windows and glass doors during the pandemic, but Municipal Code Chapter 19-2.1 gives BIAs and small businesses no pathway to use existing funds to cover the repair costs. Council is asked to request the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to explore, as part of the Municipal Code review, expanding the scope of allowable uses for existing funds.

title: Authorization to Enter into a Licence Agreement and to Waive Permit Fees Temporarily with the 519 Community Centre at Barbara Hall Park - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: fees, licences, permits; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, licenses; licensing, permit renewal
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, asks City Council to authorize a licence agreement with The 519 Church Street Community Centre at Barbara Hall Park. Barbara Hall Park, wrapping around The 519, includes greenspace, a splash pad, playground, off-leash dog area, and the AIDS and Trans Memorials. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to negotiate and sign a nominal-fee licence agreement with The 519 to facilitate programming in the park, and to waive permit fees temporarily.

title: Request for Various Exemptions for Canada Day Celebrations at Mel Lastman Square on July 1, 2022 - by Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: exemptions; exceptions
brief: Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, asks City Council to grant the permissions and exemptions needed for Canada Day celebrations at Mel Lastman Square on July 1, 2022. The Economic Development and Culture Division is producing the free, accessible, family-friendly celebration in Ward 18, with site activations, musical performances, and community programming. Council is asked to permit the use of open flames and special-effect pyrotechnics at the event.

title: Street Vending Permit Transfer to Josifina Sharif - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: permits, street vending; boulevard vending; curb lane vending; curblane vending; food carts; food vending carts; hot dog carts; sidewalk vending; vending, permit renewal
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, asks City Council to transfer a street vending permit to Josifina Sharif. Amir and Josifina Sharif have operated a hot dog cart at the corner of St. George and Bloor since 1998, the family's main source of income; Amir recently passed away, and Josifina seeks the permit in her name. Despite the prohibition on transferring Sidewalk Vending Permits in section 740-31 of Chapter 740, Street Vending, Council is asked to direct the Executive Director of Municipal Licensing and Standards to transfer the permit to her.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Above 5 Percent Cash-in-lieu Funds to the Downtown Yonge Business Improvement Area for the Rehabilitation of the Trinity Square Park Clock Tower - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: business improvement areas, funding, parks; bia; business improvement associations, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, asks City Council to release Section 42 above-5-percent cash-in-lieu funds to the Downtown Yonge Business Improvement Area for rehabilitating the Trinity Square Park clock tower. In October 2019 (MM10.10) Council approved a construction agreement and donation from the Downtown Yonge BIA, which would fund restoring the 1980s-era clock tower with up to $100,000 of its own funding and handle the design. Council is asked to amend the Parks, Forestry and Recreation 2022-2031 capital budget to create a Trinity Square Park Clock Tower sub-project.

title: 43 Russell Hill Road - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: appeals, municipal officials; city officials
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body in opposition to the minor variance applications for 43 Russell Hill Road (A1029/21TEY and A0320/21TEY). The applications seek to alter the existing three-storey detached dwelling. Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor and appropriate staff to oppose the applications at the appeal body.

title: Garden Suites - Request for Staff to meet with Alliance of Resident and Ratepayer Associations - By Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, asks City Council to direct staff to meet with the Alliance of Resident and Ratepayer Associations about garden suites. In February 2022 Council adopted Official Plan Amendment 554 authorizing residential units in ancillary buildings not adjacent to a public lane, and enacted Zoning By-law 101-2022 to give effect to it. Council is asked to direct appropriate staff, including the City Solicitor and the Chief Planner or their delegates, to meet with the Alliance on a without-prejudice basis.

title: Housing Now Initiative - 158 Borough Drive - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: housing, parking facilities; homes; residences
brief: Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson, asks City Council to advance the Housing Now Initiative at 158 Borough Drive. The City-owned parking lot at 158 Borough Drive (140, 15, 158, and 169 Borough Drive) is one of six sites Council approved in May 2020 for Phase Two of Housing Now in Ward 21, Scarborough Centre; the concept envisions about 645 housing units on the mixed-use site. Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor, with the Chief Planner, to seek an expedited Ontario Land Tribunal hearing process on the appeal of By-law 268-2022.

title: Running the Elevated Segment of Eglinton Crosstown West Extension Underground - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: light rail transit, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, lrt
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, asks City Council to push for running the elevated segment of the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension underground. The Province and the City agreed in February 2020 to deliver four priority transit projects, including the westerly extension of the Eglinton Crosstown, which runs underground from Mount Dennis Station and surfaces west of Weston Road. Council is asked to request, through the Executive Director of Transit Expansion, that Metrolinx assess burying the elevated segment and identify options.

title: Request to Waive Fees for Centennial Park Stadium in Support of Ukraine Relief Effort - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: parks, parks permits; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday, asks City Council to waive fees for Centennial Park Stadium in support of Ukraine relief. FC Ukraine United organized a fundraiser soccer game between Ukraine United Soccer Club and Olimpia Toronto on May 15, 2022 at Centennial Stadium in Etobicoke, with all proceeds planned for the BCU Foundation, which supports war casualties and their families. Council is asked to delegate authority to the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to issue the permit to FC Ukraine United at no cost, in line with the City's Refugee Resettlement Program goals.

title: 7 Ferncroft Drive - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, asks City Council to authorize the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's decision approving the minor variances in application A0027/22SC for 7 Ferncroft Drive. The application sought to alter an existing detached dwelling. Council is asked to authorize the City Solicitor to appeal the decision, attempt to negotiate a settlement, and attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body in opposition.

title: 37 Allister Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Mark Grimes
topics: appeals, municipal officials; city officials
brief: Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Mark Grimes, asks City Council to direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body in support of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of minor variance applications A0195/21SC and A0196/21SC at 37 Allister Avenue. The applications seek to permit construction that the committee refused. Council is asked to authorize the City Solicitor, with appropriate staff or outside consultants, to support the refusal and oppose the applications.

title: Renewing the District of Jaffna - City of Toronto Memorandum of Understanding - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: community outreach, public relations; awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach, publicity
brief: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to endorse extending the District of Jaffna-City of Toronto Memorandum of Understanding for a two-year term. The District of Jaffna requested the extension; Toronto is home to Canada's largest Sri Lankan and Tamil communities, with over 30,000 people of Tamil origin, many from Jaffna. The two cities remain positioned to learn from each other and work together on issues of common interest. Council is asked to endorse the extension and reiterate its commitment to the collaboration.

title: Accepting a Donation from Martingrove Baseball Inc. for Improvements to the Baseball Diamond at Silver Creek Park - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Mark Grimes
topics: parks, sports; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Mark Grimes, asks City Council to authorize accepting a $160,000 donation from Martingrove Baseball Inc. for capital work to refurbish the baseball diamond at Silver Creek Park. Martingrove Baseball, an Etobicoke league operating since 1958, offers baseball programming for children and youth aged 4 to 28 and teaches good sportsmanship in a safe, fun environment. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept the donation.

title: Amending TE26.9 regarding 245-285 Queen Street East, 348-410 Richmond Street East, 88-106 Ontario Street, and 8-12 Brigden Place - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: official plan amendments;
brief: Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, asks City Council to amend its July 2021 decision on the rental housing demolition application for 245-285 Queen Street East, 348-410 Richmond Street East, 88-106 Ontario Street, and 8-12 Brigden Place (TE26.9, application 17 160339 STE 28 RH). Part 2 of the decision authorized the Chief Planner to act on the application. Council is asked to amend the decision as set out in the motion.

title: Protecting Terrace Gardens Seniors Residence - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: seniors, seniors housing; elderly; geriatric; older adults; senior citizens
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Mayor John Tory, asks City Council to help protect the Terrace Gardens seniors residence. Terrace Gardens is a retirement home in the heart of Toronto's Jewish community providing culturally sensitive, supportive rental housing — 62 units, 34 staff, and over 72 customized programs and events each year for Jewish seniors. Council is asked to request the City Manager and the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat to explore every possible means to help keep the residence operating.

title: Acceptance of On-site Parkland Dedication Secured Through Development Application at 40 and 44 Broadway Avenue - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: applications, development; application process, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to accept the on-site parkland dedication secured through the development application at 40 and 44 Broadway Avenue. In October 2020 (NY18.5) Council accepted the settlement under which the owner will dedicate a 396-square-metre on-site park with frontage on Broadway Avenue to satisfy parkland dedication requirements. Council is asked to approve a development charge credit against the Parks and Recreation component of the development charges for the owner's design and construction of above-base park improvements.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto District School Board for J R Wilcox Community School Playground and Schoolyard Revitalization - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: funding, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, financing
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to release $350,000 in Section 37 funds to the Toronto District School Board for the J R Wilcox Community School playground and schoolyard revitalization. The playground and schoolyard are well used by the school and the community, and the funding will help build a new playground and improve outdoor areas. Council is asked to increase the 2022 approved operating budget for Non-Program by $350,000 gross and $0 net (cost centre NP2161), funded by Section 37 funds from the development at 859, 861, and 875 Eglinton Avenue West.

title: Inclusion of Affordable Housing in Development Applications - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, asks City Council to require affordable housing to be considered in all City development applications. Housing affordability and supply remain a City priority, with partnerships, collaboration, and site activation underway across Toronto for affordable and supportive housing. Council is asked to direct the CreateTO Board, Corporate Real Estate Management, and any other City agency or corporation submitting development applications that do not include affordable housing to include an explanation in their applications and reports.

title: Exploring Municipal Solutions to the Housing Crisis in Toronto - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: community crisis response, housing; crisis response, homes; residences
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to explore municipal solutions to the housing crisis. There is broad consensus Toronto is in a severe housing crisis, with residents across almost all income brackets and family types priced out or unable to afford suitable rentals — but no consensus on how to fix it or which level of government is most responsible. Council is asked to request the Chief Planner, with the Housing Secretariat, Toronto Building, the City Solicitor, and CreateTO's Chief Executive Officer, to report back on what the City can do.

title: Incentivizing Multi-Unit Homes: Improving Access to Neighbourhoods and Supporting Aging in Place - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to explore incentives for multi-unit homes to improve neighbourhood access and support aging in place. Many older homeowners are now over-housed with empty bedrooms — the Canadian Centre for Economic Analysis estimates over 5 million empty bedrooms in Ontario, likely a significant share in Toronto — and the motion seeks to incentivize single-family homes adding more units. Council is asked to request the Chief Planner, with the City Solicitor and the Chief Building Official, to report to the Planning and Housing Committee in the second quarter of 2023 on incentives.

title: 22 Ninth Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals, municipal officials; city officials
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to authorize the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's decision approving the minor variance at 22 Ninth Street (A0152/22EYK). The application proposed building a second and third storey above the existing structure. Council is asked to authorize the City Solicitor, with appropriate City staff, to appeal the decision and attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the application.

title: Supporting the City's Food Incubator Tenancy Program - by Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: business start-up, food; business incubator; business start up; entrepreneurship support; startups, menus
brief: Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to support the City's Food Incubator Tenancy Program. In May 2021 Council approved the program at 5200 Yonge Street to help start-up food entrepreneurs, prioritizing members of traditionally disadvantaged communities, but operations were delayed several times past the original 2021 start. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture and the Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management to provide $110,625 in rent abatement for additional rent payable from December 2021 to June 2022.

title: Evaluating Seabin Installation in Etobicoke-Lakeshore - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: garbage, waterfronts; food containers (waste); household garbage; plastic bags (waste); polystyrene (waste); residual solid waste; residual waste; styrofoam (waste); trash, lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to evaluate Seabin installation in Etobicoke-Lakeshore. The shoreline gets a significant amount of litter washing up; Seabins attach to seawalls or floating docks and use a pump to pull water and trash into a collection basket. Council is asked to request PortsToronto to assess the feasibility of expanding its Seabin Program to install Seabin trash-collecting devices along the Etobicoke-Lakeshore waterfront.

title: Authorization to Accept an In-Kind Donation and Enter into Agreements with Native Child and Family Services of Toronto at Eastview Park - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: First Nations; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Mayor John Tory, asks City Council to authorize accepting an in-kind donation of a shade pavilion at Eastview Park from Native Child and Family Services of Toronto, and to enter into the related agreements. Native Child and Family Services — a registered charity and one of the City's leading service organizations, with programs in Mount Dennis, Malvern, downtown, and Scarborough's Galloway neighbourhood — offers the pavilion to support its Scarborough Youth Program's outdoor activities. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept the donation and sign the agreements.

title: Enhancing Winter Accessibility to Toronto Island Park For All - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: accessibility, parks; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to improve winter access to Toronto Island Park, one of the City's most treasured destinations, attracting 1.4 million visitors a year. The park is most heavily used in summer but increasingly enjoyed in winter, and expanding all-season use has come up throughout the Toronto Island Master Plan process. Council is asked to request the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to convene a Winter Island Access Working Group, with Technology Services, other divisions, and the Ward 10 office, to provide recommendations.

title: Actions to Prevent Auto Theft - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: automobiles, theft; cars; used automobiles; used cars
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to act on the exponential increase in auto thefts in Toronto, Ontario, and Quebec in 2022. Council has previously requested the Federal and Provincial Governments to provide resources to the Toronto Police Service to combat this crime and requested the Province to establish a Provincial/Municipal Auto Theft Task Force. Council is asked to request the Federal and Provincial Governments to work with the automotive and insurance industries on additional anti-theft measures.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 funds to fund the Production and Installation of a Heritage Plaque to Recognize Dr. Anderson Abbott - by Councillor Mike Layton seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: funding, plaques; financing, heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, asks City Council to release $7,500 in Section 37 funds to Heritage Toronto for a heritage plaque recognizing Dr. Anderson Abbott. Anderson Ruffin Abbott (1837–1913) was the first Canadian-born Black doctor, and also an educator, journalist, hospital administrator, coroner, and poet; born in Toronto to free Black parents, he served as a surgeon in the American Civil War. Council is asked to increase the 2022 approved operating budget for Heritage Toronto by $7,500 gross and $0 net, funded by Section 37 community benefits.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 funds to fund the Production and Installation of a Heritage Plaque to Recognize Donald Willard Moore - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: funding, plaques; financing, heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, asks City Council to release $4,250 in Section 37 funds to Heritage Toronto for a heritage plaque recognizing Donald Willard Moore. Donald Willard Moore (1891-1994) was a leader in Toronto's Black community and a civil rights activist who fought to change Canada's exclusionary immigration laws; born in Barbados, he came to Canada and became a prominent organizer. Council is asked to increase the 2022 approved operating budget for Heritage Toronto by $4,250 gross and $0 net, funded by Section 37 community benefits.

title: Waiving Development Charges and Other Fees to Support the Construction of the Blackhurst Cultural Centre - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: culture (sc), development; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, asks City Council to waive development charges and other fees to support construction of the Blackhurst Cultural Centre. The purpose-built centre, led by A Different Booklist Cultural Centre in partnership with the City of Toronto, will provide permanent, affordable, accessible space for Black artistic and cultural production in Toronto. Council is asked to waive site plan fees for the new cultural centre at 756 Bathurst Street and authorize waiving any other City fees connected to its development and construction.

title: Authorization to Accept and Approve A Development Charge Credit for the Design of the Future Park at 840-860 Dupont Street - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: development, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, asks City Council to authorize accepting and approving a development charge credit for the design of the future park at 840-860 Dupont Street. Council previously authorized a parkland dedication of about 700 square metres from the development, being built as part of a residential project just north of Christie Pits. Council is asked to approve accepting the on-site parkland dedication as authorized in item 2016.CC17.1, adopted March 31-April 1, 2016, and to grant the development charge credit for the park's design.

title: Protecting Community Input in the Planning Process - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: community outreach, planning & development (sc); awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, asks City Council to protect community input in the planning process. The established process has City staff review development applications, followed by a community consultation meeting before a final report goes to Council, but recent changes to the Ontario Planning Act have pressured Toronto to review applications faster. Council is asked to request the Province of Ontario to amend the Planning Act or the Ontario Land Tribunal Act so any applicant who appeals for lack of a decision must hold a community consultation meeting with City Planning and the local councillor.

title: Parking commercial plated 24 hour service vehicles on driveways in residential zones - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: parking, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to review the zoning prohibition on driveway parking of commercial vehicles in residential neighbourhoods. Council is asked to request the Chief Planner, with Municipal Licensing and Standards, to review the regulations restricting outdoor parking of commercially licensed vehicles on private property.

The school and community need an accessible playground meeting Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act standards, with safe design for Kindergarten to Grade 8 students and public outdoor access. Council is asked to increase the 2022 approved operating budget for Non-Program by $150,000 gross and $0 net (cost centre NP2161), funded by Section 37 funds from the development at 743 Weston Road area.

title: Support for Bill C-233, “Keira’s Law” - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: abuse, female; assault; domestic violence; violence, female only; women only; women
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, asks City Council to support MP Anju Dhillon's private member's Bill C-233, “Keira's Law”. Violence against women is a Canadian public health crisis — one in four women experience domestic violence in their lifetime, and on average one woman or girl is killed every other day; the pandemic worsened the crisis, and the National Judicial Institute notes there is no mandatory domestic-violence education for judges. The bill would amend the Criminal Code and Judges Act to strengthen protections for women and children. Council is asked to support the bill.

title: City of Toronto Endorsement of Bill 60, the Safe and Healthy Communities Act (Addressing Gun Violence), 2022 - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: community safety;
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to endorse Bill 60, the Safe and Healthy Communities Act (Addressing Gun Violence), 2022. The bill amends the Health Insurance Act so insured services include prescribed hospital- and community-based violence intervention programs and trauma-informed counselling for survivors and others affected by gun violence; it also amends the Health Protection and Promotion Act so boards of health must run programs to reduce gun violence. Council is asked to endorse the bill.

Council is asked to approve the funding.

title: Adjustments to Capital Budget, Carry Forward Funding and Future Year Commitments

title: Tree Removal Permit Appeals - Delegation to Community Council

title: Considering All Growth-Related Funding Tools at Executive Committee

brief: Mayor John Tory asks City Council to temporarily change its procedures so the Executive Committee can consider all growth-related funding tools together.
