Council is asked to suspend the necessary rules until November 14, 2022 so the Executive Committee can hold the statutory public meetings on these charges.

brief: This is an information item: the Board of Governors of Exhibition Place considered item EP23.9 on April 5, 2022 and recommends City Council approve extending the exclusive food and beverage services agreement with Spectra Food Services for the Enercare Centre and other trade and consumer show buildings, except the Beanfield Centre. Spectra won the contract through a 2013 public tender; the extension would add five years, December 1, 2024 to November 30, 2029, on the same terms except updated financial terms. Council is asked to approve the extension.

title: Amendment to the Master Agreement with the Canadian National Exhibition Association and City of Toronto to Provide for a One Year Extension
brief: This is an information item: the Board of Governors of Exhibition Place considered item EP23.3 on April 5, 2022 and recommends City Council approve a one-year extension of the First Renewal Term of the master agreement with the Canadian National Exhibition Association, from April 1, 2022 to March 31, 2023. The parties would then negotiate the Second Renewal Term starting April 1, 2023. Council is asked to approve the extension.

title: St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts Redevelopment - CreateTO
brief: The CreateTO Board asks City Council to endorse the building program for a reimagined St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts at 27 Front Street East, as itemized in Attachment 2 to the March 23, 2022 report. Under Council's January 2020 direction (EX12.6), CreateTO and TO Live prepared the building program, Class D cost estimate, business model, and funding strategy for the civic asset. Council is asked to endorse the building program.

title: ConnectTO Program Update
brief: Staff update the Executive Committee on phase one of ConnectTO, the program to centralize stewardship of municipal resources and assets to advance the City's equity and connectivity goals, which Council approved in February 2021. The Deputy City Manager of Corporate Services and the Chief Technology Officer recommend City Council endorse the proposed creation of a City-owned high-speed fibre Municipal Broadband Network to support municipal services and connect City-owned facilities and assets. The Executive Committee is asked to recommend that Council endorse the next steps.

title: Commercial Property Ownership Mechanisms in Little Jamaica
topics: businesses, commercial properties, commercial tenants, neighbourhoods; commercial waste collection customers, cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods, office real estate; retail space
brief: The Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee asks City Council to direct the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration and the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture, in consultation with others, to act on commercial property ownership mechanisms in Little Jamaica. The advisory committee considered item CR6.3 at its April 1, 2022 meeting, where Black UrbanismTO presented financial structures to increase Black commercial property ownership. Council is asked to approve the direction.

title: Feasibility of Restrictions on the Retail Sale and Public Use of Consumer Fireworks and Responses to Outstanding Directives
brief: This is an information item: the Fire Chief and the Executive Director of Municipal Licensing and Standards report to the Economic and Community Development Committee on the feasibility of restricting the retail sale and public use of consumer fireworks, responding to Council directives from May through July 2021. The report updates actions taken against unpermitted and illegal fireworks use, public education during the 2021 warm-weather season, and plans for 2022. Council is asked to direct the Fire Chief to take further action.

title: Toronto Action Plan to Confront Anti-Black Racism - Year Three Update
brief: This is an information item: the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration presents the Year Three update on the Toronto Action Plan to Confront Anti-Black Racism to the Economic and Community Development Committee. Council unanimously adopted the five-year plan — 80 actions and 22 recommendations — on December 5, 2017 to drive systems change against the legacy of anti-Black racism. The committee is asked to request the City Manager, with the Executive Director and General Manager, to continue the work.

title: Renewing Participation in the Community Data Program
brief: Staff ask City Council to renew the City's participation in the Community Data Program — a national partnership of municipalities and non-profit, community-based organizations that collectively acquire and share sociodemographic, disaggregated, place-based data. The partnership is the City's primary source of disaggregated, neighbourhood-level Census data, needed for sound social and community planning. The Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration recommends Council authorize entering into a community-based partnership agreement. Council is asked to approve the renewal.

title: Selected Grants and Community Service Partnerships Extensions
brief: Staff ask City Council to delegate authority to the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration to allocate Community Service Partnerships funding. Throughout the pandemic, non-profits, grassroots, and resident-led groups took vital leadership roles serving vulnerable Torontonians, and the division provided over $65 million in 2020 and 2021 to support the social service sector. The report also covers extensions to selected grants. Council is asked to approve the delegation.

title: Changes to the Upper Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management
brief: This is a procedural item: staff ask City Council to approve changes to the Upper Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management, in accordance with Municipal Code Chapter 19, Business Improvement Areas. Council is asked to approve the board changes.

title: Jane Finch Initiative - Ideas Report and Community Development Plan Phase 2
brief: Staff ask City Council to advance the Jane Finch Initiative's Ideas Report and Community Development Plan Phase 2. The resident-informed initiative plans the future of the Jane and Finch area (Neighbourhood 24 Black Creek and Neighbourhood 25 Glenfield-Jane Heights) through two integrated plans — a Secondary Plan and a Community Development Plan — to support residents, local groups, and businesses as the area changes. Council is asked to request the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration and the Interim General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to proceed with Phase 2.

title: Vacancies in the Offices of Councillor, Ward 10, Spadina-Fort York and Ward 13, Toronto Centre, and Contingency Plan for Any Further Vacancies
topics: councillors, replacement; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council
brief: The City Clerk asks City Council to deal with vacancies in the offices of Councillor for Ward 10, Spadina-Fort York, and Ward 13, Toronto Centre, and a contingency plan for further vacancies. Councillor Joe Cressy resigned effective April 30, 2022, and Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam resigned effective May 4, 2022; another vacancy could arise depending on the outcome of the June 2, 2022 Ontario general election. The City Clerk recommends Council declare both seats vacant and schedule a special meeting for Wednesday, June 1, 2022 at 9:30 a.m. to appoint replacements, plus a contingency plan. Council is asked to declare the vacancies and set the meeting.

The City continues to face significant, unprecedented financial impacts from the pandemic — added costs and revenue losses — totalling an anticipated $1.4 billion in 2022 across all City programs and agencies, per the Council-approved 2022 Operating Budget. They recommend Council receive the report for information. Council is asked to receive the report. No decision is attached.
