brief: Staff recommend the Bid Award Panel award the landscaping contract (Ariba document 3333466537) for Area 1 to Municipal Maintenance Inc. and for other areas to Forest Ridge Landscaping Inc. Three bids were received, with bid prices including Forest Ridge Landscaping at $2,415,323 and Lima's Gardens & Construction at $2,120,870; Municipal Maintenance Inc. was the recommended supplier for Area 1. The panel is asked to grant the awards.

title: Staffing Matters - Fourth Quarter 2021 Update, Cost of Living and Initial First Quarter 2022 Update
topics: equity; employment equity; fair wage; pay equity
brief: Staff update the CreateTO Board of Directors on staffing, including a snapshot of human resources at the end of the fourth quarter of 2021, a recommendation for a 2022 cost of living adjustment, and an early first-quarter 2022 update. The CEO recommends the Board approve and implement the cost of living adjustment for the 2022 fiscal year. The Board is asked to approve the adjustment.

title: 2022 Annual Performance Objectives - Chief Executive Officer
topics: work plans;
brief: Staff present the CreateTO Chief Executive Officer's performance objectives for 2022, along with compensation and HR matters. The CEO recommends the Board of Directors approve the annual objectives as outlined in the March 17, 2022 report and handle the confidential compensation details appropriately. The Board is asked to approve the 2022 objectives.

title: Mount Dennis Campus Opportunity
topics: land, planning & development (sc); property
brief: Staff ask the CreateTO Board of Directors to recommend that City Council authorize CreateTO to pursue a post-secondary campus opportunity in Mount Dennis. Council asked CreateTO to identify lands in the Mount Dennis area suitable for a post-secondary campus; the CEO recommends the Board direct CreateTO and City staff to engage in a collaborative exercise with a local post-secondary school to review the feasibility of a campus project. Council would authorize the CEO, in consultation with the City Manager and other officials, to proceed.

title: Housing Now - Selection of Proponent for Bloor-Kipling (Six Points), Block 1 (5207 Dundas Street West)
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: Staff ask the CreateTO Board of Directors to approve the recommended proponent, identified in Confidential Attachment 2, for the development and operation of affordable and rental housing at the Housing Now Bloor-Kipling (Six Points) Block 1 site at 5207 Dundas Street West. In October 2021, CBRE launched the market offering on behalf of the Housing Secretariat and CreateTO. The Board is asked to approve the proponent and direct the CEO, with the Housing Secretariat, on next steps.

title: Housing Now Business Case for 158 Borough Drive
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: Staff ask the CreateTO Board of Directors to endorse the business case and market offering for the Phase 2 Housing Now site at 158 Borough Drive. The 1.57-acre site is an underutilized property currently holding a structured parking facility serving the Scarborough Civic Centre, on the north side of the precinct. The Board is asked to endorse the business case in Confidential Attachment 1, subject to further approvals by the Deputy City Managers, CFO, and others.

title: Housing Now Progress - Update
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: This is an information item: the Vice President of Development gives the CreateTO Board of Directors a verbal update on progress on the Housing Now Initiative since the previous board meeting, and reports on the approach used to establish a successful Community Benefits Plan for the Housing Now sites. No decision is attached.

title: St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts Redevelopment
topics: redevelopment, theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: This is an information item: the President and CEO of TO Live updates the CreateTO Board of Directors on the reimagined St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts at 27 Front Street East. Under Council's January 2020 direction (EX12.6), CreateTO and TO Live are preparing a building program, Class D cost estimate, business model, and funding strategy for the civic asset. The Board is asked to receive the update.

title: Action Items and New Matters Referred by City Council
topics: council items; clauses; items (council); items before council
brief: This is an information item: staff update the CreateTO Board of Directors on action items from prior meetings and on matters City Council has directed CreateTO to become involved in since the previous board meeting. The Board is asked to receive the update for information.

title: Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer Drug Strategy
topics: harm reduction, lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgendered; crack kits; methadone clinic; methadone maintenance; methadone treatment; needle exchanges; safer crack kits; safer crack smoking materials; safer injection, gay community; glbt; homosexual; lgbt; queer; transexual; transgendered; two spirited
brief: City Council asks the Board of Health to direct the Medical Officer of Health and the Associate Director of the Toronto Drug Strategy Secretariat to create a specific Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer Drug Strategy as part of the Toronto Drug Strategy. Council considered item EX29.7 on February 2-3, 2022 and made recommendations to the Board of Health. The Board is asked to approve the direction.

title: Climate Change and the Role of Public Health
topics: climate change, public health; climate protection
brief: This is an information item: the Medical Officer of Health reports to the Board of Health on climate change and the role of public health. The report covers the mandate of Toronto Public Health and the Medical Officer of Health under the Health Protection and Promotion Act and the Ontario Public Health Standards' mandatory health programs and services. The Board is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Health Impacts of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Children and Youth
topics: children, public health, youth; adolescents, child
brief: The Medical Officer of Health updates the Board of Health on the health impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on school-age children and youth, including current Toronto Public Health programs supporting them, in response to the Board's earlier request. The Board is asked to request the Medical Officer of Health to work with the Province of Ontario and Toronto school boards on further research and a baseline assessment of youth mental health and well-being, to measure the performance of future interventions. The Board is asked to approve the direction.

title: TO Supports: COVID-19 Equity Action Plan Update
topics: equity, public health; employment equity; fair wage; pay equity
brief: This is an information item: the Medical Officer of Health and the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration update the Board of Health on the TO Supports: COVID-19 Equity Action Plan. Toronto Public Health and the City committed from the start of the pandemic to identifying and mitigating inequities in health outcomes, and in December 2020 the Board endorsed the plan with 25 targeted equity actions. The Board is asked to receive the update for information.

title: Response to COVID-19 - April 2022 Update
topics: disease outbreaks, public health; epidemics; pandemics
brief: This is an information item: the Medical Officer of Health gives the Board of Health a presentation on the April 2022 COVID-19 response update. No decision is attached.

title: Danforth Avenue Planning Study (Segment 2 - Don Valley to Coxwell Avenue) - City-Initiated Official Plan Amendment and Urban Design Guidelines - Final Report
topics: Official Plans, avenue study, official plan amendments;
brief: Staff recommend City Council adopt a City-initiated Official Plan Amendment with a Site and Area Specific Policy, plus urban design guidelines, for Danforth Avenue from the Don Valley in the west to Coxwell Avenue in the east. The Danforth Avenue Planning Study (Segment 2) aims to support the historic main street's character — its walkable shopping, gathering spaces, small businesses, and local jobs — while planning for future growth, following Council's 2014 direction to study the avenue. Council is asked to adopt the amendment and guidelines.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council reviews the Order Paper. No decision is attached.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions, and announcements are made at the City Council meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions. No decision is attached.

title: Declarations of Interests
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council declare interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. No decision is attached.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: the Mayor and committee chairs introduce the committee reports and new business from City officials for the Council meeting, including deferred items and the reports of the Executive, Audit, Board of Health, Economic and Community Development, General Government and Licensing, and Infrastructure and Environment committees. No decision is attached at this step.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council confirms the minutes from its special meeting held on March 9, 2022. No other business is attached.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Council meeting opens with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: Toronto Heritage Survey Phase One and Heritage Planning Process Update
topics: economic development, heritage conservation districts, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Planner updates City Council on Phase One of the Toronto Heritage Survey, responding to Council's July 2019 request for a progress report and timeline. Delayed by the pandemic and by Bill 108 changes to the Ontario Heritage Act, the survey is now established as a foundation of good planning to give transparency about where properties have heritage interest, alongside revisions to heritage planning processes. Council is asked to request a further report in the third quarter of 2023, after Phase One's work plan is complete, with recommendations on future phases.

title: Response to the Provincial Consultation on Partial and Phased Occupancy of Super-Tall Buildings
topics: buildings, high rise buildings; tall buildings
brief: The Chief Building Official asks City Council to respond to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing's consultation on whether the Building Code should allow partial and phased occupancy of “super-tall” buildings still under construction, and what those requirements should be. Tall buildings have been part of Toronto's landscape since the early twentieth century, but as towers get taller and construction takes longer, the Province is seeking input. Council is asked to request that the Minister convene a task force of construction site safety experts.

title: Response to City Council's Directions Arising from the Toronto Local Appeal Body Chair's 2020 Annual Report
topics: delegation of authority, local government structure; city council structure; committee structure; council committee structure; council structure; council-committee structure; governance structure, signing authorities
brief: Staff respond to City Council's direction to report back by the first quarter of 2022 on the Toronto Local Appeal Body (TLAB), covering its operations relative to its original intent, simplifying hearings and increasing public participation, compensation for the Chair and Vice-Chair for review-request hearing time, the Chair's role in annual budget preparation, and fee amendments. The Deputy City Manager recommends Council approve increasing TLAB membership from ten to fourteen part-time members including a Chair and Vice-Chair, and approve a half-day per diem rate for the Chair and Vice-Chair for review request hearings. Council is asked to approve the changes.

title: 778 King Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the property at 778 King Street West under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The two-storey brick building with stone trim, just west of Tecumseth Street, is a representative mid-twentieth-century industrial headquarters in the Streamlined Moderne style — designed by Leo Hunt Stanford and built in 1947 for the York Mending Wool Company, later home to Uniforms Registered and the Ydessa Hendeles Art Foundation gallery (1988-2017). Council is asked to state its intention to designate in line with the statement of significance.

title: 2726 and 2734 Danforth Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the two adjacent listed properties at 2726 and 2734 Danforth Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, for their cultural heritage value. On the north side of Danforth Avenue east of Main Street and west of Dawes Road in the East End-Danforth neighbourhood, the area is tied to early European settlement at Dawes' Corners, later the village of Little York, the Town of East Toronto (1903-1908), and eventually Toronto. Council is asked to state its intention to designate 2726 Danforth Avenue (entrance at 2732) and 2734 Danforth Avenue.
address: 2726 Danforth Toronto Ontario; 2734 Danforth Toronto Ontario

title: 68 Kendal Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the listed heritage property at 68 Kendal Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, for its design, historical/associative, and contextual values. On the west side of Kendal Avenue north of Jean Sibelius Square in the Annex, the property contains the Audley Court Apartments, designed by architect Joseph Hunt Stanford for contractor and developer C. R. S. Dinnick — a fine early example of Toronto apartment architecture in the Edwardian style. Council is asked to state its intention to designate in line with the statement of significance.

title: 14 Duncan Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the property at 14 Duncan Street (including entrance addresses at 180, 184, and 188 Pearl Street) under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. On the northwest corner of Duncan and Pearl streets in King-Spadina, the property contains the Telfer Paper Box Building — a three-storey Edwardian Classical structure on a raised basement, built in 1902 by the Telfer Manufacturing Company to the designs of architects Gregg and Gregg and occupied for 60 years by the Telfer Paper Box Company. Council is asked to state its intention to designate in line with the statement of significance.

title: 10 and 10A Dawes Road - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend City Council affirm its July 14-16, 2021 decision (DM35.1) stating its intention to designate the properties at 10 and 10A Dawes Road under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The City received an objection to the notice of intention from an interested party within the statutory timeline; staff reviewed the objections and found they have no bearing on the properties' cultural heritage value. Council is asked to affirm the designation intention and authorize the City Solicitor on next steps.
address: 10 Dawes Toronto Ontario; 10A Dawes Toronto Ontario

title: Housing Now - 140, 150, 156, 158 and 160 Borough Drive - City Initiated Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-Law Amendment - Final Report
topics: redevelopment, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve City-initiated Official Plan and zoning by-law amendments for the City-owned parking lot at 158 Borough Drive (140, 150, 156, 158, and 160 Borough Drive), one of six sites Council approved in May 2020 for Phase Two of the Housing Now Initiative. The concept would transform the parking lot in the heart of Scarborough Centre's Civic Precinct into a mixed-use site with rental housing including affordable units, a daycare, and an improved and expanded public realm. Council is asked to amend the Official Plan and Employment Districts Zoning By-law 24982.
address: 140 Borough Toronto Ontario; 150 Borough Toronto Ontario; 156 Borough Toronto Ontario; 158 Borough Toronto Ontario; 160 Borough Toronto Ontario

title: 824 Sheppard Avenue West, 177, 179 and 181 Cocksfield Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition and Conversion Application - Final Report
topics: demolitions, official plan amendments, redevelopment, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a 12-storey, 44.95-metre mixed-use building at 824 Sheppard Avenue West and 177, 179 and 181 Cocksfield Avenue, with 19,932 square metres of gross floor area — including 459 square metres of retail and a 373 square metre daycare — at a floor space index of 4.0. The proposal includes 263 residential rental units and 197 parking spaces, and would demolish existing buildings containing 15 rental units, with all 15 replaced within the new building. Council is asked to amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law 569-2013 and approve the rental housing demolition and conversion.
address: 177-179 Cocksfield Toronto Ontario; 824 Sheppard Toronto Ontario

title: Authorization for Submission of Minor Variance Application 411 Victoria Park Avenue and 2510 and 2530 Gerrard Street East - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: applications, minor variances; application process, variance
brief: Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to authorize submission of a minor variance application for 411 Victoria Park Avenue and 2510 and 2530 Gerrard Street. Under the Planning Act as amended by Bill 73, minor variance applications are barred within two years of a privately-initiated zoning by-law amendment unless Council declares by resolution that one is permitted; Council approved zoning amendments for the site in July 2021 (By-law 959-2021). Council is asked to authorize the application for relief from minimum parking space requirements.
address: 2510 Gerrard Toronto Ontario; 2530 Gerrard Toronto Ontario; 411 Victoria Park Toronto Ontario

title: 5 Marina Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday, asks City Council to direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose an appeal for 5 Marina Avenue. The applicant sought Committee of Adjustment consent to sever the property into two undersized residential lots for a new semi-detached dwelling on each, plus four variances from lot frontage, lot area, floor space, and parking space width requirements under Zoning By-law 569-2013; City Planning staff recommended refusal. Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor, with appropriate staff, to oppose the appeal.

title: Re-Opening of Item EY27.12 - Parking Amendments - La Rose Avenue - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Mark Grimes
topics: parking;
brief: Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Mark Grimes, asks City Council to re-open item EY27.12, adopted in November 2021, which prohibited parking at all times on the north side of La Rose Avenue between a point 100 metres east of Timothy Court and a point 20 metres further east. Underground utilities found in the boulevard prevent installing sign posts where originally planned, so Transportation Services recommends shifting the prohibition to between 80 metres and 150 metres east of Timothy Court. Council is asked to delete its previous decision and prohibit parking at all times on the north side of La Rose Avenue from 80 metres east of Timothy Court to 70 metres further east.

title: Seeking Provincial Funding for the Construction of Riverine Flood Mitigation for the  Rockcliffe-Smythe Area - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: flooding, funding; financing, floods
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Mayor John Tory, asks City Council to seek provincial funding for riverine flood mitigation construction in the Rockcliffe-Smythe area of Ward 5 (York South-Weston). The area is the most flood-vulnerable in the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority's jurisdiction, with hundreds of buildings in the Black Creek and Lavender Creek regulatory floodplain facing frequent surface and basement flooding from riverine flooding and overloaded urban drainage. Council is asked to direct the City Manager to review opportunities and request provincial funding, along with federal funding, for the recommendations in the Rockcliffe Riverine Flood Mitigation Environmental Assessment.

title: Support for the Grange Green Plan - by Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: green standards, greenhouse effect, reserve funds; green development standards; sustainable development standards; toronto green standards, greenhouse gas emissions, reserves and reserve funds
brief: Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to release Section 37 funds to the Sir William Campbell Foundation, the non-profit that maintains and operates Campbell House Museum, for the next phase of the Grange Green Plan. The plan aims to improve public green space, enhance private greening efforts, and advance the City's environmental and climate agenda for the Grange community's human and ecosystem health. Council is asked to increase the 2022 Council-approved operating budget for Non-Program on a one-time basis by $15,000 gross and $0 net, funded by Section 37 community benefits from developments at 40-60 McCaul Street and 10 Stephanie Street.

title: Aligning City Procurement with Federal Sanctions - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
brief: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to align City procurement with federal sanctions in support of the Ukrainian people and to ensure the City does not contribute to Russia's aggression. After learning that governments had entered agreements with people and firms linked to Russian oligarchs, the motion seeks to prevent the City from doing the same, without affecting previous agreements. Council is asked to amend Municipal Code Chapter 195, Purchasing, to incorporate sanctions into the Supplier Code of Conduct.

title: Release of Section 37 Funds from various developments to MABELLEarts for Capital Improvements to Mabelle Parkette - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: development, funding, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, developing land; development (land); land development, financing
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, asks City Council to release $500,000 in Section 37 and Section 45(9) Planning Act funds to MABELLEarts for capital improvements to Mabelle Parkette, which the motion says are urgently needed. MABELLEarts has also been awarded over $700,000 from the federal revitalization program for the project. Council is asked to increase the Council-approved 2022 operating budget for Non-Program by $500,000 gross and $0 net on a one-time basis, fully funded by the Section 37 and 45(9) funds.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 1580 Avenue Road to Community Matters Toronto for Mural Art on Bell Utility Boxes in Eglinton-Lawrence - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: funding, urban beautification; 20-minute makeover; beautification projects; clean & beautiful city; clean and beautiful city; clean city beautiful city; community clean-up days; facade improvement; mural program; neighbourhood beautification, financing
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, asks City Council to release Section 37 funds from the development at 1580 Avenue Road to Community Matters Toronto for the Bell Box Murals Project. Since 2009, artists with the project have painted murals on Bell Canada utility boxes, replacing graffiti with original local art. Council is asked to increase the approved 2022 operating budget for Non-Program by $13,500 gross and $0 net on a one-time basis, funded by the Section 37 funds for park and streetscape improvements in the area.

title: Release of Section 37 Funds to Support the Purchase of Permanent Office and Community Meeting Space for the Toronto Aboriginal Support Services Council in Regent Park - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: First Nations, aboriginal services, community benefits, funding; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, financing
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to release Section 37 funds to support the Toronto Aboriginal Support Services Council's purchase of permanent office and community meeting space. The council is a Toronto-based coalition of 18 Indigenous social services agencies serving Indigenous people in Ward 13 Toronto Centre and across the city, which lost its official office and meeting space in 2020. Council is asked to increase the 2022 Council-approved operating budget for Non-Program by $650,000 gross and $0 net on a one-time basis, funded by Section 37 community benefits from the development at 88 Queen Street East and 10 Mutual Street.

title: Release of Section 37 funds to the St. Lawrence Market Neighbourhood BIA for streetscape and public realm improvements in the St. Lawrence Community - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: business improvement areas, funding, neighbourhoods; bia; business improvement associations, cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods, financing
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to release $400,000 in Section 37 funds to the St. Lawrence Market Neighbourhood BIA to complete streetscape improvements. The site plan for 154-158 Front Street East was approved in 2012, and Council has since approved improvements to the pedestrian boulevards of Front Street East and the St. Lawrence public realm. Council is asked to approve the release.

title: 1500-1536 St. Clair Avenue West and 20-36 Caledonia Road - Authorizing Staff to Seek Off- Site Park Dedication in Respect of Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Applications - by Councillor Ana Bailão, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The applicant filed Official Plan and zoning by-law amendment applications (21 175097 STE 09 OZ, deemed complete June 25, 2021) for 1500-1536 St. Clair Avenue West and 20-36 Caledonia Road. Parks staff asked for an on-site parkland dedication, which the applications do not show; the applicant provided a rationale for off-site parkland dedication instead. Council is asked to authorize staff to seek off-site parkland dedication for the development.
address: 1500 - 1536 St Clair Toronto Ontario; 20 - 36 Caledonia Toronto Ontario

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item MM39.30 regarding Sublease to Thunder Woman Healing Lodge Society at 161 Spadina Road to Provide Affordable Transitional Housing to Indigenous Women - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: housing, women; homes; residences, shelters for women
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, asks City Council to re-open and amend item MM39.30 to let the Thunder Woman Healing Lodge Society perform state-of-good-repair and Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act compliance work at 161 Spadina Road. The City leases the premises from the Province under a 99-year lease expiring November 30, 2083, which permits subleasing; the society would do the work to City standards at an estimated cost of $400,000 exclusive of taxes, on the City's behalf and at the City's expense, to provide affordable transitional housing for Indigenous women. Council is asked to amend Attachment 1 to permit the work.

title: Release of Section 37 Funds for Upkeep of the Zhong Hua Men Chinese Archway in Ward 14 - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: funding, reserve funds; financing, reserves and reserve funds
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to release Section 37 funds for upkeep of the Zhong Hua Men Chinese Archway in Ward 14. The archway at Broadview Avenue and Gerrard Street East — the gateway to East Chinatown, opened in fall 2009 as a joint project of the City and the Chinese Chamber of Commerce (East Toronto), with land and construction management from the Toronto Parking Authority — needs ongoing maintenance. Council is asked to transfer $27,426 from the Section 37 reserve fund for the 90-100 Broadview Avenue development (source account XR3026-3700348) to the Chinese Archway Reserve Fund (XQ4220).

title: Protecting Existing Housing and Creating Permanently Affordable Homes with Supports for Youth at 556 Bathurst Street - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: affordable housing, housing, youth; adolescents, affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Mayor John Tory, asks City Council to protect existing housing and create permanently affordable homes with supports for youth at 556 Bathurst Street. With affordable multi-unit properties being lost to sale and redevelopment, the motion seeks to preserve existing affordable homes and create permanently affordable options for lower-income residents, including those experiencing homelessness — with an immediate opportunity to support Youth Without Shelter and Terra House North Toronto Emergency and Referral Agency. Council is asked to authorize the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat to provide $3 million, inclusive of HST and disbursements, from the Capital Revolving Reserve Fund for Affordable Housing (XR1058).

title: Authorization to release Section 37 funds from the development at 4 and 6 Tippett Road to Community Matters Toronto for painting Mural Art on 15 Bell Utility Boxes in York-Centre - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: development, funding; developing land; development (land); land development, financing
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to release Section 37 funds from the development at 4 and 6 Tippett Road to Community Matters Toronto for the Bell Box Murals Project. Since 2009, artists with the project have painted murals on Bell Canada utility boxes across Toronto and beyond, replacing graffiti with original art, making streets more inviting, reflecting local culture, and giving residents accessible public art. Council is asked to increase the approved 2022 operating budget for Non-Program by $22,500 gross and $0 net on a one-time basis, fully funded by the Section 37 funds for local improvements in Ward 10 (now Ward 6).
address: 4 Tippett Toronto Ontario; 6 Tippett Toronto Ontario

title: Massey Hall Revitalization: City of Toronto Support - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam
topics: entertainment, redevelopment; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, asks City Council to support Massey Hall's revitalization with a City loan guarantee. Opened in 1894, Massey Hall is Canada's most celebrated music venue; its 2018-launched revitalization will expand its capacity to serve audiences, develop artists, and act as a cultural and tourism hub — contributing $348 million to the local economy and 4,000 jobs through construction and the first five years of operations, then $42.6 million annually with 430 full-time-equivalent jobs and 500,000 visitors. Council is asked to approve the loan guarantee to Massey Hall's lender on an exceptional basis to complete the capital financing.

title: Modernizing Black Creek Pioneer Village to Prioritize Indigenous Perspectives - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: First Nations; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, asks City Council to modernize Black Creek Pioneer Village with an emphasis on prioritizing Indigenous perspectives. The village has been a cornerstone Toronto attraction since 1960, and as the City's first Reconciliation Action Plan moves forward, the motion seeks to reimagine the heritage site — educating the public about First Nations, Inuit, and Métis history in Toronto and establishing a forward-looking vision. Council is asked to request the City Manager, with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, to report back on June 15, 2022 on the funding required.

title: Entering into Encroachment Agreements with the University of Toronto to Accelerate the Implementation of District Energy Systems - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: encroachments, energy; energy resources; energy use
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, asks City Council to support encroachment agreements with the University of Toronto to accelerate district energy systems. U of T's St. George Campus Climate Positive Plan depends on decarbonizing its district energy system and connecting more buildings, which requires 12 underground road crossings for thermal energy piping that the City must permit; the current permitting process for non-utilities is onerous and uncertain. Council is asked to support the underground street-crossing encroachment agreement and direct the Executive Director of Energy and Environment, the TTC Board, and Transportation Services on next steps.

title: 399 Bathurst Street (Toronto Western Hospital) - University Health Network's Request for Minister's Zoning Order - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: hospitals, zoning;
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Mayor John Tory, asks City Council to support the University Health Network's request for a Minister's Zoning Order for Toronto Western Hospital at 399 Bathurst Street. The hospital — a leading acute-care academic centre for neurosurgery, cancer, and transplant care — faces aging infrastructure: the 100-year-old Main Pavilion and 51-year-old McLaughlin Pavilion cause incidents and surgical delays affecting patient care. Council is asked to adopt the Chief Planner's March 30, 2022 recommendations, including supporting a Neighbourhood Relations Committee of hospital, community, and City representatives.

title: 2022 COVID-19 Intergovernmental Funding Update - Urgent Funding Commitments Required - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: disease outbreaks, funding; epidemics; pandemics, financing
brief: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, asks City Council to seek urgent COVID-19 funding commitments from other governments. When Council approved the 2022 operating budget on February 17, 2022, the City faced $1.4 billion in pandemic-related financial pressures with minimal confirmed support; significant federal and provincial announcements since have cut the shortfall by a third, but a gap remains. Council is asked to adopt the City Manager and CFO's April 5, 2022 recommendations requesting the governments of Canada and Ontario to allocate 2022 COVID-19 operating support.

title: 699 Sheppard Avenue East - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, asks City Council to amend the zoning for 699 Sheppard Avenue East, revisiting the parking supply secured when Council approved the site's redevelopment as a mixed-use 12-storey building in July 2021 (NY25.2). After Council's approval, the applicant proposed re-evaluating the parking supply, and in January 2022 North York Community Council directed the Director of Community Planning, with Transportation Services, to review it. Council is asked to adopt the Chief Planner's April 5, 2022 recommendations amending Zoning By-law 7625 for the lands.

title: 1573 Bloor Street West - Liquor Licence Application - Capones Cocktail Lounge License Number 1627551 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: applications, liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, application process
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor sales licence for Capones Cocktail Lounge at 1573 Bloor Street West (licence 1627551) is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns are attached. The indoor-only application is near residential units, with concerns about noise, litter, safety, and other disturbances to residents. Council is asked to direct the City Clerk to advise the AGCO registrar accordingly.

title: 1570 Bloor Street West - Liquor Licence Application for Bawara - Licence 1541731 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: applications, liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, application process
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor sales licence for Bawara at 1570 Bloor Street West (licence 1541731) is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns are attached. The application covers an indoor area and a small outdoor area proposed on the City boulevard, near residential units, with concerns about noise, litter, safety, and other disturbances. Council is asked to direct the City Clerk to advise the AGCO registrar accordingly.

title: Authorization to enter into a Licence Agreement with The Neighbourhood Group and Aki Wiidookaagewin (Earth Helpers) at Spadina Museum - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam
topics: licences, museums (facilities); licenses; licensing
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, asks City Council to authorize a licence agreement with The Neighbourhood Group and Aki Wiidookaagewin (Earth Helpers) at Spadina Museum. In June 2021 the City, Aki Wiidookaagewin (Ontario Earth Helpers), The Stop Community Food Centre, and the Alexandra Park Neighbourhood Learning Centre signed a memorandum of understanding for the Indigenous Kitchen Garden Project — raised bed gardens at Spadina Museum demonstrating food-growing practices and creating employment and skills training for Indigenous peoples. Council is asked to ratify the memorandum retroactively and authorize the licence agreement.

title: 785 Annette Street - Liquor Licence Application for Queen Margherita Pizza - License 1611279 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor sales licence for Queen Margherita Pizza at 785 Annette Street (licence 1611279) is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns are attached. The indoor-only application is near residential units, with concerns about noise, litter, safety, and other disturbances. Council is asked to direct the City Clerk to advise the AGCO registrar accordingly.

title: 37 Wilket Road - Representation at Toronto Local Appeal Body Appeal Hearing - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals, hearings;
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to direct the City Solicitor and appropriate staff to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing for 37 Wilket Road and oppose the Committee of Adjustment's approval. In March 2022 the North York panel approved a consent to sever the through-lot — which has a backyard on Bayview Avenue — into two undersized lots plus associated minor variances, and a third party appealed to the tribunal. Council is asked to authorize the City Solicitor's attendance to oppose the approval.

title: Release of Section 37 Funds to the Scarborough Food Security Initiative for Capital Improvements to the Scarborough Heights Allotment Garden - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: food, funding; financing, menus
brief: Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, asks City Council to release Section 37 funds to the Scarborough Food Security Initiative for capital improvements to the Scarborough Heights Allotment Garden. The 0.45-acre garden on Toronto and Region Conservation Authority land south of Glen Everest Road, managed by the City and long used by residents of 10 Glen Everest Road and neighbours, has drawn numerous complaints over the years. Council is asked to increase the 2022 Council-approved operating budget for Non-Program on a one-time basis by $16,000 gross and $0 debt, funded by Section 37 community benefits from the 2229-2245 Kingston Road development.

title: EmpowerTO: It’s time to Free Toronto from the Ontario Land Tribunal - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam
topics: planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, asks City Council to call on the Province of Ontario to dissolve the Ontario Land Tribunal and replace it with a true appeals body that only grants hearings based on an error in law or procedure. The motion describes the tribunal as an unelected, unaccountable quasi-judicial body with the final say over planning matters, whose provincially appointed chairs need no background in land use planning, and notes no other city Toronto's size has so little control over its own planning future. Council is asked to approve the request to the Province.

title: Re-Opening and Amending IE26.10 Regarding Palmerston Square and Tecumseth Street - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy
topics: bike paths, bikeway networks; bicycle facilities; bicycle routes; bike routes; bikeway routes; bikeways; cycling routes; shared roadways; signed routes, bicycle paths; bicycle trails; bike trails; cycling paths; cycling trails; off-road paths (cycling)
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Joe Cressy, asks City Council to re-open and amend its December 2021 decision (IE26.10) authorizing new bikeways on Palmerston Avenue, Palmerston Square, Palmerston Boulevard, and Tecumseth Street. Since December, staff have consulted local councillors and stakeholders — including a January 31, 2022 meeting with three business owners on Tecumseth Street — and the motion seeks to change the approved installation and by-law amendments. Council is asked to amend its previous decision by deleting parts 2.b. and 2.e. and authorizing the revised bicycle lane installations.

title: Examining the Regulatory Framework that covers Life Lease Housing and whether opportunities exist to include it as a form of Affordable Housing - by Councillor Cynthia Lai, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
brief: Councillor Cynthia Lai, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, asks City Council to examine the regulatory framework for life lease housing and whether it could count as affordable housing. Life lease housing is the right to occupy a unit for a set period, often a lifetime — increasingly marketed to seniors as a cheaper alternative to buying a comparable condo — but pre-construction life lease projects do not follow all the same rules as pre-construction condos and lack Tarion coverage, raising purchaser-protection concerns. Council is asked to direct the Chief Planner and the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat to report to the Planning and Housing Committee in the first quarter of 2023.

title: Expanding Canoe Landing Park Under the Gardiner Expressway - by Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
brief: Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to expand Canoe Landing Park under the Gardiner Expressway. Canoe Landing Park, at the heart of the heavily used CityPlace neighbourhood, packs a children's playground and splash pad, a fenced off-leash dog area, grass and artificial-turf sports fields, and landmark public art like the Red Canoe into a small space — and for apartment dwellers the local park is their backyard. Council is asked to request the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to include a Canoe Landing Park expansion project under the Gardiner in future budget submissions within the 10-year capital plan.

title: Transfer of Funds for the City of Toronto's Commitment to the New YMCA Facility at 505 Richmond Street West - by Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
brief: Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to fund the City's commitment to the new YMCA facility at 505 Richmond Street West. The historic Waterworks Building near King and Spadina is being redeveloped with new affordable housing, a youth shelter, heritage conservation, expanded parkland, and market housing and commercial uses — including a 54,000-square-foot YMCA built in partnership with the YMCA. Council is asked to amend the 2022-2031 capital budget and plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation to create a new capital sub-project, 505 Richmond YMCA Funding, with a project cost of $21,147,179.

title: Green Future Forward: Establishing an Effective Governance and Operating Model for Allan Gardens and the Palm House Conservatory - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: gardens, green standards; green development standards; sustainable development standards; toronto green standards
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to review the governance and operating model for Allan Gardens and the Palm House Conservatory. Allan Gardens Park and Conservatory has been a Toronto park destination for over 150 years — a place of social change, protest, and community gathering in the Garden District — and its conservatory is one of three municipally owned conservatories, a complex of six glasshouses each with its own climate and plant collection including exotic orchids and tropical plants. Council is asked to direct the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to establish a review process in consultation with park users and stakeholders.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 (Planning Act) Funds to Enhance Community Safety and Engagement in the Moss Park Neighbourhood by supporting Growing Neighbourhoods Foundation (Building Roots) - by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: funding, neighbourhoods; cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods, financing
brief: Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to release $100,000 in Section 37 funds to the Growing Neighbourhoods Foundation (Building Roots), a non-profit serving the downtown east and Moss Park neighbourhood. Founded in 2013 as a grassroots social venture responding to lack of fresh food access and growing space, the foundation would use the funds to build capacity for programming promoting social cohesion and a safer community environment. Council is asked to increase the 2022 Council-approved operating budget for Non-Program by $100,000 gross and $0 net, funded by Section 37 funds from the 154 Front Street East development.

title: Authorization to enter into a Licence Agreement with The Neighbourhood Group Community Services and Aki Wiidookaagewin (Earth Helpers) at Paul Martel Park - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam
topics: licences, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, licenses; licensing
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, asks City Council to authorize a nominal-fee licence agreement with The Neighbourhood Group Community Services and Aki Wiidookaagewin (Earth Helpers) at Paul Martel Park. The 1,030-square-metre park in the Bloor-Spadina neighbourhood, a City park since 2003 renamed in 2014 for community champion Paul Martel, would host Indigenous participant training in collaboration with the park's stewardship community. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to negotiate and sign the agreement.

title: Release of Section 45(9) Funds from the Development at 75 Canterbury Place to CaterToronto for Capital Improvements to the Existing Restaurant Incubator Space at 5200 Yonge Street - by Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: development, funding; developing land; development (land); land development, financing
brief: Councillor John Filion, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to release Section 45(9) Planning Act funds to CaterToronto for capital improvements to the restaurant incubator space at 5200 Yonge Street. The City is helping new food entrepreneurs from culturally diverse communities through City-owned retail space at 5200 Yonge Street, with the program launching later in April 2022 and outdoor cooking grills planned on adjacent City property; CaterToronto, a non-profit chosen by the City, helps new food entrepreneurs. Council is asked to increase the 2022 Council-approved operating budget for Non-Program by $30,000 gross and $0 debt, funded by Section 45(9) funds from the 75 Canterbury Place development.

title: Achieving Community Benefit Agreements on Major Transit Projects - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: projects, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, asks City Council to reconfirm its commitment to Community Benefit Agreements on major transit infrastructure projects. Community Benefit Agreements, increasingly used by governments across North America, maximize social and economic impacts of public construction — with Ontario's movement built on community and labour working together so the people building public infrastructure reflect local community demographics. Council is asked to reconfirm its ongoing commitment and recognize the importance of the initial ground-breaking Community Benefit Agreement for the Eglinton Crosstown LRT.

title: Supporting the Continued Implementation of the Bathurst Quay Neighbourhood Plan - by Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: neighbourhoods, neighbourhoods (planning); cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods
brief: Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to support continued implementation of the Bathurst Quay Neighbourhood Plan, approved in 2017 after more than two years of consultation to revitalize the derelict City-owned property with new public spaces and repair the heritage-designated Canada Malting Silos into a cultural and community services hub. The City and partners — the residents' association, business community, Canada Ireland Foundation, Waterfront Neighbourhood Centre, Ports Toronto, and the Toronto District School Board — have advanced the vision, with first-phase public space construction starting in October 2019. Council is asked to increase the 2022 capital budget for the Toronto Waterfront Revitalization Initiative by $419,520.98 gross and $0 debt for the Bathurst Quay Public Realm subproject, funded by Section 37.

title: Advancing the Legacy Art Project Inspired by Terry Fox- by Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton
topics: art programs; art classes; art workshops; arts programs
brief: Councillor Joe Cressy, seconded by Councillor Mike Layton, asks City Council to advance the citizen-funded Legacy Art Project memorial to Terry Fox at 439 Queens Quay West, between the Spadina Wetlands and the Toronto Music Garden — a site Council endorsed in July 2018 (MM44.38). A design has been chosen: “We Are Shaped by the Obstacles We Face” by Jon Sasaki and DTAH, appearing as the iconic silhouette of Fox mid-stride from the installation's west end, with hundreds of thousands of dollars raised in private donations. Council is asked to amend the 2022-2031 capital budget and plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation to create a new capital sub-project, LAP Terry Fox, with a project cost of $340,907.

title: Authority to Allocate Funding and Execute an Agreement with Elevate Toronto - by Councillor Michael Thompson, Mayor John Tory
topics: funding, programs; financing
brief: Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Mayor John Tory, asks City Council to allocate funding to Elevate Toronto. Founded in 2017 as an annual technology festival, Elevate drew over 15,000 attendees, 300 speakers and performers, and 150 international media in 2019, with 250 start-ups and companies at its job fair — now Canada's largest festival at the intersection of arts and tech; the reimagined 2022 festival runs September 20-22, 2022. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to allocate up to $350,000 to Elevate in 2022 for community programming including the festival, and to negotiate the agreement.

title: Advancing Justice Centres in Toronto - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: funding; financing
brief: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson, asks City Council to advance Ontario's Justice Centre pilots in Toronto. The community courts co-locate justice, city, health, and social services so participants work with on-site social, health, mental health, addictions, and housing providers for holistic wrap-around support — aiming to reduce recidivism and improve outcomes for Toronto's most justice-involved, high-needs communities; the City and the Ministry of the Attorney General are piloting two centres, Toronto North West and Toronto Downtown East. Council is asked to authorize the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration to extend agreements with the Ministry to receive $304,130.

title: Extending the Green Market Acceleration Program into 2023 - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: green standards, programs; green development standards; sustainable development standards; toronto green standards
brief: Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson, asks City Council to extend the Green Market Acceleration Program to March 31, 2023. Council authorized the program in May 2018 (ED29.4) for four years, with the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture and the Director of the Toronto Office of Partnerships to report back at the end of the period; the four-year term ends in May 2022. Council is asked to authorize the extension and delegated authority to execute agreements.

title: Addressing Nuisance Watercraft - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: pests, water; nuisance animals; vermin
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to address nuisance watercraft on Lake Ontario. Personal watercraft and vessel use has increased, with reports of dangerous operation, speeding too close to shore, and intrusion into environmentally sensitive areas harming wildlife — and negligent operation has caused deaths and injuries in Toronto. Council is asked to request the City Manager to report back on opportunities to enhance waterfront safety from the Rouge River to Etobicoke Creek, including in-water speed signage, educational campaigns, and coordinated enforcement.

title: Establishing a Framework to Address Abandoned Boats - by Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: vessels; boats
brief: Councillor Mark Grimes, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, asks City Council to establish a framework for quickly addressing abandoned boats at public boat launches, public docks, or attached to City property. In February 2021 an abandoned boat left over the winter in Humber Bay Park West sank into Lake Ontario, and in March 2022 another sank at Bluffers Park, raising environmental concerns about pollutants and wildlife, with public confusion over who to report abandoned boats to. Council is asked to direct the City Manager and relevant divisions to develop the framework.

title: Concept 2 Keys Dashboard and Updates at Planning and Housing Committee Meetings - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão
topics: affordable housing, planning; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ana Bailão, asks City Council to require a Concept 2 Keys dashboard at each remaining Planning and Housing Committee meeting this term. The Concept 2 Keys Priority Development Review Stream, launched as a pilot in January 2021 to prioritize and expedite affordable housing approvals amid the housing crisis, was directed by Council in October 2021 to expand. Council is asked to request the City Manager's Chief of Staff to report a dashboard listing all current Concept 2 Keys projects and their progress to each remaining committee meeting.

title: Supporting the Bloor-Yorkville Business Improvement Area Purchase of New Seating in the Village of Yorkville Park - by Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam
topics: business improvement areas, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, business improvement associations; BIA
brief: Councillor Mike Layton, seconded by Councillor Kristyn Wong-Tam, asks City Council to support the Bloor-Yorkville Business Improvement Area's purchase of new seating for the Village of Yorkville Park. In January the BIA bought additional tables and seating — unique to the park and matching its existing infrastructure — so they could be installed before warm weather, as park use surged during the pandemic. Council is asked to increase the 2022 Council-approved capital budget for Economic Development and Culture on a one-time basis by $18,000 gross and $0 debt, funded by Section 37 funds.

title: Chapter 918 - Parking on Residential Front Yards and Boulevards - Technical Amendment
topics: boulevards, by-laws, change, minor variances, municipal codes, municipal officials, parking, parking pads, planning, property owners, transportation, zoning; amendments; conversion; modification, boulevard grass, boulevard parking; front yard parking; off street parking; off street permit parking, building owners; land owners; property ownership, bylaws, city officials, transportation services, variance
brief: This is a technical housekeeping item: the General Manager of Transportation Services asks City Council to amend Section 918-3A of Municipal Code Chapter 918, Parking on Residential Front Yards and Boulevards, responding to a Planning and Housing Committee request to protect Council's authority to regulate front yard parking. The amendment deletes the phrase “or any other by-law provision” and adds “, except as” after “under this chapter”. Council is asked to approve the technical amendment.

title: Developing a Parking Strategy for Toronto
topics: city initiatives, climate change, parking, transportation; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, climate protection, transportation services
brief: This is an information item: the General Manager of Transportation Services proposes a framework for developing a city-wide Parking Strategy for Toronto. The strategy would position parking as part of an integrated transportation network that sustains decades of growth while meeting the greenhouse gas reduction targets set by TransformTO, drawing on several City partners with parking-related mandates. Council is asked to receive the framework report for information.

title: Cycling Network Plan - 2022 Cycling Infrastructure Installation - First Quarter and 2021 ActiveTO Cycling Network Expansion Project Updates
topics: bike lanes, bikeway networks, cycling, infrastructure; bicycle facilities; bicycle routes; bike routes; bikeway routes; bikeways; cycling routes; shared roadways; signed routes, bicycle lanes; on street bike lanes, bicycling
brief: The General Manager of Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize installing 10 centreline kilometres of new bikeways in 2022-2024, as part of the Cycling Network Plan and Near Term Implementation Plan Council adopted in December 2021. The near-term projects, with design and consultation complete, include the Bartlett-Havelock-Gladstone cycling connections from Davenport Road to College Street, and Council authority is needed for the installation plus the related Chapter 886, 903, 910, 925, and 950 by-law amendments. Council is asked to authorize the installations.

title: Donation from The Garden Club of Toronto for Allan Gardens Children's Conservatory Teaching Garden Renovations
topics: children, conservatories (greenhouses), donation, environmental education, gardens; bequest; toy drive, water education programs
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize accepting a donation of up to $0.100 million from The Garden Club of Toronto, a registered charity, to support revitalizing the Allan Gardens Children's Conservatory Teaching Garden. The City's 2022-2031 Capital Budget and Plan already includes $0.250 million in debt funding in 2022 for the garden renovations, and Council authority is needed to amend the capital plan to increase the total project cost. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept the donation and enter into a donor agreement.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Alfa Laval Incorporated, Pro Aqua, Incorporated and Veolia Water Technologies Canada Incorporated, for the Purchase of Proprietary Essential Parts for Maintenance of Process Equipment at Various Wastewater and Water Treatment Plants for Toronto Water
topics: contracts, maintenance, operating budgets, purchasing, wastewater treatment plants, water treatment; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants, water filtration; water purification
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize the General Manager of Toronto Water to negotiate and enter into three non-competitive contracts — with Alfa Laval Incorporated, Pro Aqua, Incorporated, and Veolia Water Technologies Canada Incorporated — for proprietary parts and supplies to maintain process equipment at the City's wastewater and water treatment plants. Each contract would run from issuance to March 31, 2023, with options to renew for six additional one-year periods at the City's discretion, subject to budget approvals. Council is asked to grant the authority.

title: January 16 and 17, 2022 Major Snow Event, Post-Operational Report
topics: snow advisory reports, snow emergencies, snow management, winter storms; de-icing; snow clean-up; snow plans, snow emergency
brief: This is an information item: the General Manager of Transportation Services reports to City Council on the January 16-17, 2022 major snow event, when 55 centimetres of snow fell in just 15 hours amid extreme cold, with below-freezing temperatures lasting more than two weeks afterward. The response required extraordinary efforts beyond normal salting and plowing, involving Transportation Services, Strategic Communications, 311, and Fleet Services. Council is asked to request a report to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee in the first quarter of 2023 on an Extreme Winter Weather Response Plan, developed with internal and external stakeholders.

title: Parking Amendments - Victoria Park Avenue
topics: change, community councils, costs, funding, operating budgets, parking, parking prohibitions, signs, transportation; amendments; conversion; modification, financing, no parking, signage, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council amend the parking prohibition on the west side of Victoria Park Avenue, north of Queen Street East. Because the street borders two community council areas, Council approval is required. The change would extend the existing all-times parking prohibition by 8 metres further north — from a point 90 metres north of Queen Street East to 38 metres beyond that point — covering the section between two closely spaced driveways to keep sightlines clear for motorists. Council is asked to approve the amendment.

title: Bringing a Public Health Lens to Indoor Ventilation Requirements
topics: heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, public health; air conditioning; air conditioning systems; boilers; climate control systems; cooling systems; furnaces; heat; heating systems; hvac; ventilation; ventilation systems
brief: Dr. Kate Mulligan and Councillor Joe Cressy ask City Council to bring a public health lens to indoor ventilation requirements. Better indoor ventilation can reduce the spread of respiratory infectious diseases — a lesson widened by the COVID-19 pandemic — but many ventilation dimensions sit outside municipal jurisdiction, and Toronto Public Health lacks deep in-house technical expertise. Council is asked to request that Municipal Licensing and Standards and Toronto Building review the latest knowledge and best practices for ventilation to reduce infectious disease transmission.

title: Non-competitive Agreement with Ford Motor Company of Canada Limited for Original Equipment Manufacturer Parts and Services through their Authorized Dealer Network
topics: agreements, city vehicles, operating budgets, purchasing, service delivery, vendors; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize the General Manager of Fleet Services to negotiate and enter into a non-competitive agreement with Ford Motor Company of Canada Limited, giving the City access to its dealer network through the Ford Fleet Care program for proprietary Ford original equipment manufacturer parts and services, plus parts discounts through the National Fleet Part Pricing program. The authority would also cover non-competitive agreements with individual Ford authorized dealers under both programs. Council is asked to grant the authority.

title: ServiceNow Procurement Issue Update
topics: legal matters, licences, municipal officials, printing and distribution, purchasing, technology acquisition; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, circulation; copying; mailing list; photocopying; printing; subscriptions, city officials, information technology acquisitions; it acquisitions, legal issues, licenses; licensing
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Procurement Officer, Chief Technology Officer, and City Solicitor update City Council on the approach to addressing the situation with Deloitte in connection with the award of ServiceNow subscription licences (GL28.6, awarded to Fully Managed Incorporated for non-exclusive supply of ServiceNow cloud subscription services). Staff recommend Council direct that Confidential Attachment 1 to the March 8, 2022 report remain confidential in its entirety. Council is asked to keep the attachment confidential.

title: Emergency Non-competitive Contract with AECOM Canada Limited, and Amendment to Purchase Order 6045596 for Repairs to the East Don Sanitary Trunk and Highland Creek Sanitary Trunk Sewers
topics: by-laws, capital budgets, change, contracts, emergencies, municipal codes, purchasing, repairs, sanitary sewers, taxes, trunk sewers; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, amendments; conversion; modification, bylaws, levies, main sewers; sewer mains
brief: This is an information item: staff advise City Council, under the Purchasing By-law, of an emergency non-competitive contract with AECOM Canada Limited for engineering design and contract administration for emergency repairs to the East Don Sanitary Trunk Sewer and the Highland Creek Sanitary Trunk Sewer, valued at $650,000 inclusive of contingency and net of all applicable taxes and charges ($661,440 net of HST recoveries). The report also covers an amendment to purchase order 6045596 with Capital Sewer Services Incorporated for full-length trenchless rehabilitation work. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Amendments to Municipal Code Chapter 217, Records, City (Corporate)
topics: archives (records), by-laws, digitization, municipal codes, municipal officials, records, schedules; bylaws, city officials, digital imaging; scanning, project schedules; scheduling; timing
brief: The City Clerk asks City Council to amend Municipal Code Chapter 217, Records, Corporate (City), to support the City's transition to digital recordkeeping. The amendment would establish a new records retention schedule specifically for email, which would prevail over any other retention schedule, as set out in Attachment 1 to the March 8, 2022 report. Council is asked to approve the amendment.

title: Status of Audit Recommendations and Key Cybersecurity Risks

title: Revisiting Legacy Rental Replacement Policies to Align them with the City's Affordable Rental Housing Expectations
topics: affordable housing, audits; affordable homes; housing projects, auditors; auditors
brief: The Auditor General asks City Council to revisit the City's legacy rental replacement policies so they align with the City's affordable rental housing expectations. The Official Plan aims to preserve affordable rental stock, and Municipal Code Chapter 667 requires that where redevelopment would lose six or more rental units, the same number of rental units be replaced — but older agreements may not reflect current affordability expectations. Council is asked to direct the Chief Planner, in consultation with the City Solicitor and other divisions, to report back through the Planning and Housing Committee on the merits of amending the policies.

brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the property at 1702 Queen Street East under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. On the northwest corner of Queen Street East and Kingston Road in the Woodbine Beach precinct, the property contains the Imperial Bank of Canada Building — a two-storey bank building on a raised basement with a one-storey wing, built in 1911-12 as an Imperial Bank of Canada branch to the designs of Toronto architects Sharp & Brown, with classical ornamentation. Council is asked to state its intention to designate in line with the statement of significance.

brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the property at 50 Merton Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The Girl Guides of Canada Headquarters there was the organization's first permanent, purpose-built national headquarters since its founding in Canada in 1910 — a three-storey complex completed in 1962 to the design of Carmen Corneil for William J. McBain & Associates and extended in 1970-72 by Elin and Carmen Corneil, recognized as a significant work of Post-War Modern architecture. Council is asked to state its intention to designate in line with the statement of significance.

title: Our Plan Toronto: Update on Growth Plan Conformity and Municipal Comprehensive Review
topics: growth;

title: Mandatory Pre-Application Consultation: Recommended Amendments to the Official Plan and to the Municipal Code - Final Report
